articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers ride key hits and excellent defense to win Game 1 of the World Series
articles.summary: The Brewers held on for a dramatic 3-2 win after Tampa Bay threatened in the ninth inning. They lead the best-of-seven World Series, 1-0.
articles.body:
• The Brewers take Game 1: Two runs in the first inning and an insurance run in the seventh were all Milwaukee needed to take the first game of the 2026 World Series, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 3-2.

• Stars come through: Milwaukee’s captain, Christian Yelich, and star catcher William Contreras got things started quickly with big hits off Rays starter Nick Martinez. Five solid innings from Jacob Misiorowski and a lockdown performance from the Brewers bullpen sealed the win.

• A tense ending : A fairly straightforward game turned dramatic in the ninth inning when the Brewers appeared to turn a double play to end things with the bases loaded. Replay showed that shortstop Cooper Pratt pulled his foot off second base and the call was overturned, scoring a run.

• One hit short: A clutch strikeout by Trevor Megill on Jonny DeLuca ended things on the next at-bat, with the tying run left on third.

Our live coverage has ended. Scroll through the posts below to read more.

Baseball fans who suspected this matchup of small market teams had the potential to produce a thrilling World Series were proven right in Game 1 in Milwaukee as the Brewers took the opening game of the best-of-seven series 3-2 at American Family Field.

The tale of the tape on the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays is very similar. Both teams may lack the household names of some of their opponents with much higher payrolls, but they each earned the best record in their league playing a similar brand of baseball – a team-oriented approach with relentlessly attacking offenses, strong starting pitching and shutdown bullpens.

The Brewers offense came out swinging in the first inning Friday night, touching Rays starting pitcher Nick Martinez for a pair of runs on a triple by Christian Yelich followed by a single from William Contreras.

Milwaukee leaned on its flame-throwing ace Jacob Misiorowski, who made those two runs stand up as he worked five innings and earned his first career postseason win as a starter.

The Rays cut the Brewers’ lead in half in the fourth inning with an RBI groundout from catcher Liam Hicks, but the Miz was able to avoid any further damage and stranded the tying run on third base to hold the score at 2-1.

Milwaukee added to its lead in the seventh inning with a clutch, two-out single from left fielder Jackson Chourio to drive in Cooper Pratt and tack on a much-needed insurance run to make the score 3-1.

After stellar bullpen work from Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby, Brewers manager Pat Murphy handed the ball over to star closer Trevor Megill for the ninth inning.

The Rays were not ready to go quietly into the Wisconsin night, and back-to-back one-out singles from Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson brought Tampa Bay’s All-Star slugger Junior Caminero to the plate representing the go-ahead run. After getting a fortunate call on a check swing that looked like it might have been strike three, Caminero drew a walk to load the bases.

Hicks then appeared to ground into an game-ending 4-6-3 double play, and the fireworks went off as the Brewers shook hands on the infield grass.

But the Rays challenged the call on the field, and on replay review, it was determined that Brewers shortstop Pratt took his foot off second base an instant too soon. The double play was overturned and pinch-runner Jorge Mateo scored to make the score 3-2 with one more out left to go.

With the smoke from the fireworks still hanging in the air, Megill gathered his composure and struck out Jonny DeLuca with a nasty breaking ball to end the game.

The two teams will meet again Saturday night for Game 2 with Tampa Bay sending its postseason ace Drew Rasmussen up against Milwaukee’s Logan Henderson.

We knew these were going to be close games.

How close? Try a couple millimeters between the bottom of the spike on the cleat of a rookie shortstop and the second base bag he was supposed to be touching when he turned a slick double-play to seemingly end the game.

In the end it didn’t matter. The Rays challenged the ninth-inning double-play call, won, and were awarded a run and another shot to stay alive.

Five pitches later, Jonny DeLuca struck out to end the game anyway.

The Brewers bullpen – perhaps their biggest strength relative to an incredibly similar Rays’ club – bends but does not break.

Rather than swing the outcome, the strange scene instead served to underscore what will likely become the themes of this entire series: Close games, action on the basepaths, determinative defense.

There were more double steals (1) than home runs (0) in the game. There were more inning-ending outs made at third base than either manager is probably happy about.

Already the “small-ball Series” reputation has started to feel a little heavy-handed. But Game 1 lived up to that billing.

National League Cy Young frontrunner Jacob Misiorowski earned his first career postseason win as a starter in front of a sellout crowd of more than 43,000 in Milwaukee in Game 1 of the World Series.

After the biggest win of his career, Misiorowski told Fox Sports, “It was amazing. Just to have this city behind me, it means the world, and behind this team, we just couldn’t ask for anything better. And I just want to say thank you.”

The fireballing Miz didn’t rack up the Ks Friday night, but he allowed just one run over five innings, scattering four hits and three strikeouts.

High drama will be the theme of this series, all the way to the very end.

Yandy Díaz got the inning started with a weak groundout but then the Rays put together a threat.

Johnathan Aranda singled and Chandler Simpson followed suit, bringing slugger Junior Caminero to the plate as the potential go-ahead run. Facing closer Trevor Megill, it was a high-stakes matchup between one of the top closers in baseball and Tampa’s up-and-coming star.

A double-steal put Aranda and Simpson in scoring position and then Caminero worked a walk to load the bases after Megill spiked a few curveballs in the dirt.

It all turned a moment later when Liam Hicks, known for his power, stepped to the plate and promptly grounded the first pitch he saw to second base. The Brewers appeared to turn the 4-6-3 double play to end things with the bases loaded.

Replay showed that shortstop Cooper Pratt pulled his foot off second base before he caught the throw from second baseman Bryce Turang. The out call at second was overturned, allowing Aranda to score from third base and put runners on second and third.

With two outs, Jonny DeLuca came to the plate and went down on strikes, waving at strike three in the dirt.

Huge exhales in Milwaukee as the Brewers hold on!

With the Rays desperately needing to hold the score right where it is, the Brewers were angling for more insurance.

Milwaukee’s hottest hitter William Contreras led off the inning with his second hit of the game - a single into left field - which led Tampa Bay to make another pitching change, this time handing the ball to Garrett Cleavinger.

Cleavinger promptly waded into deeper water by walking Brice Turang. Garrett Mitchell did the Rays a favor by getting under his bunt attempt, allowing Junior Caminero to catch it on the fly and hold the runners at first and second.

Tampa Bay thought they’d escaped when Cooper Pratt grounded into an apparent inning-ending double play, but the out at first base was overturned on review and the bottom of the eighth continued.

Brewers manager Pat Murphy then turned to veteran pinch hitter Gary Sanchez, which led to another Rays pitching change.

Cole Sulser came in for Tampa Bay and induced a 5-4 fielder’s choice, with a stellar play by Caminero to field the ball on a short-hop to end the threat and send the game to the 9th inning.

Another 1-2-3 inning for the Rays – who tried to get anything going against Aaron Ashby with a pinch hitter – and now the Rays have three outs left to mount a comeback.

And the Brewers have yet to go to their closer, Trevor Megill.

It’s a little boring to believe that bullpens win championships, but it certainly helps to feel like a two-run lead is insurmountable.

Milwaukee’s Jake Bauers’ followed Jackson Chourio’s clutch hit with a single that hit the chalk on the third base line, giving the Brewers runners on the corners with team captain Christian Yelich stepping to the plate.

Yelich smoked a line drive right at Tampa Bay first baseman Jonathan Aranda, who took the ball to the bag to end the Brewers’ rally and hold Milwaukee to just one run in the inning.

Damage done, but the Rays are still close.

Rays manager Kevin Cash sent Steven Matz out to work the seventh inning after pitching his way into and out of trouble in the sixth.

Matz issued a leadoff walk to Cooper Pratt to immediately put himself back in the pressure cooker.

Sal Frelick hit a hard liner to left, but it was hauled in by Chandler Simpson on the run. A slow roller to shortstop from David Hamilton moved Pratt into scoring position and brought Cash out to make a pitching change.

Kevin Kelly surrendered a bouncing single from Jackson Chourio into right field to bring Pratt in to score with a much-needed insurance run.

Chourio, 22, already owns the all-time Brewers postseason records for homers (6) and RBI (18) in just 20 games. In fact, that’s the most postseason homers and RBI ever by any player prior to his 23rd birthday.

Abner Uribe strikes out Junior Caminero, and then Aaron Ashby comes in to strike out Liam Hicks and induce a fly out from Jonny DeLuca and suddenly we’re at the seventh-inning stretch.

You can see why Milwaukee has felt confident playing close games and found success even without starters going deep.

Speaking of the stretch: the in-game entertainment plays “God Bless America,” “Take Me Out To The Ballgame,” and a little ditty I’ve never heard before that seems to be Milwaukee-specific. I already forgot any identifying lyrics, but the jumbotron showed an accordion player as it wound down.

The Milwaukee Brewers are deadly serious about their baseball this season.

Finishing with the best record in MLB, they’re hoping that this will be the year they can finally win a World Series after clinching a spot in the Fall Classic. But this is a franchise that doesn’t always take itself too seriously, and the bright lights of October will help showcase one of the most wonderfully ridiculous servings in sport: The slapstick sixth-inning sausage race.

It’s exactly as absurd as it sounds. Human runners, wearing 7-foot-tall foam costumes with goofy faces and colorful features depicting a Bratwurst, Polish, Italian, Hot Dog and Chorizo, race each other around home plate on the warning track. The comedically top-heavy sausages, which can easily topple forwards into the dirt, temporarily take center stage as the baseball players gaze on in amusement from their dugouts, sometimes wagering on the outcome.

We’re into the bullpens now with the game still hanging in the balance.

Tampa Bay turned to the unlikely Steven Matz, who was making just his second appearance of this postseason.

After recording two quick outs, a pair of walks to William Contreras and Brice Turang had the Brewers threatening in the bottom of the sixth.

A harmless groundout from Garrett Mitchell put an end to the rally and sends the game to the seventh inning.

For the second inning in a row, what could have been a Rays rally ends with a runner getting thrown out attempting to steal.

This time it was strike-‘em-out, throw-‘em-out double play – with Chandler Simpson the victim at the plate and Jonathan Aranda getting gunned down trying to snag second.

We knew these would likely be low-scoring games, and now we’re seeing how that can translate to more drama, not less as both teams navigate just how aggressive to get about every opportunity.

Abner Uribe comes in to pitch the sixth for the Brewers and thus ends Jacob Misiorowski’s first World Series start.

Well, somewhere between the total dominance he displayed in the regular season and the shaky starts he’s had so far this October. But even saying that is getting a little greedy in terms of what The Miz is capable of.

He set a World Series velocity record. He left with his team leading after giving up just one run. He gave a sold-out crowd of 43,250 plenty to cheer about. If I can quibble, his five whiffs on 24 fastballs for 21% is about half of the rate he was running in the regular season.

That won’t matter though if the Brewers’ bullpen – the best in the postseason with a 1.33 ERA coming into this game – can hold on to get a win.

Milwaukee’s speedy nine-hole hitter David Hamilton broke up a string of nine consecutive hitters retired for Nick Martinez, but a slight stumble on the base paths snuffed a would-be Brewers’ rally.

After ripped a ball into the right field corner, Hamilton got out of stride and nearly tripped rounding second base. The minor slowdown was all the window the Rays needed as right fielder Victor Mesa, Jr. and Ben Williamson combined for a perfect relay to get Hamilton by a split-second at third base.

The miscue meant another quick inning for the Rays as the AL champs keep trying to claw their way back against the Brewers.

We might not have an iconic individual moment yet five innings into this World Series, but the small-ball matchup is delivering on the drama that comes from simply making contact.

With Jacob Misiorowski looking like he’s battling – yes, even at 101+ – the Rays started working deep counts and seemed on the verge of something.

Victor Mesa Jr., who singled earlier in the inning, was on second and Yandy Díaz – one of the best hitters with runners in scoring position across all MLB – at the plate.

But for some reason Mesa decided he needed to be 90 feet closer to home plate and attempted to steal. Instead, he gets gunned down by William Contreras (whose arm Statcast measured at seventh-best among over 70 catchers in the regular season) to end the inning.

The Rays are usually a fundamentally sound team but you know what they say: Never make the first or third out of the inning at third.

Brice Turang brought the fans at American Family Field to their feet when he put a charge into a Nick Martinez pitch, but Rays left fielder Chandler Simpson hauled the ball in as he crashed into the wall.

Martinez then got a pair of quick groundouts and an inning that started with a bang turned into another quick inning for the Tampa Bay starter.

The Brewers had one of the better defenses during the regular season. This October, they’ve looked a little leaky.

A shot off of the bat of Junior Caminero was ruled a double – and kudos to him for his using his superlative bat speed to catch up to Misiorowski’s 101.5 mph pitch. The Rays got a bit of a break when centerfielder Garrett Mitchell misread the ball and failed to break back on the drive.

That double pushed Jonathan Arranda, who walked, to third base, and catcher Liam Hicks drove him in with a soft ground out. It’s not quite an explosion of offense, but it gets a run across for the Rays and cuts the Brewers’ lead in half.

After a couple shaky innings, Tampa Bay starer Nick Martinez settled in with a 1-2-3 third inning.

He started by striking out NLCS MVP Jake Bauers, then fanned Christian Yelich with a high heater.

Martinez then induced a popout to right field from hot-hitting William Contreras to end the inning.

In his third frame, Jacob Misiorowski mixes up his arsenal a little more.

Oh sure, he’s still topping 102 mph with his fastball, but he mixes his sliders, curveballs and a cutter to get another 1-2-3 inning.

A two-pitch out of Yandy Díaz to finish the frame keeps his pitch count in check, too. It’s good to have the guy who is basically impossible to get a hit against on the mound.

articles.title: Brewers come from behind to win Game 2 and take a 2-0 World Series lead
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers take a commanding 2-0 lead in the World Series after a 5-4 win over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 2.
articles.body:
Milwaukee takes a 2-0 World Series lead: The Brewers once again came from behind in this postseason, rallying from four runs down to for a 5-4 win in Game 2, taking a 2-0 lead in the World Series.

A wild game: The Rays opened the game with a four-run barrage in the top of the first but the Brewers came all the way back to take the lead, 5-4.

New Brewer heroes: Sal Frelick’s home run in the bottom of the sixth tied the game and Cooper Pratt drove in a run in the seventh for another Brew Crew postseason comeback.

Tension all the way to the end: The opening game of the series went all the way down to the final pitch as both teams played up to expectations. Game 2 was more of the same as it went all the way down to the final pitches and the Rays, once again, left the tying run on base.

Our coverage of Game 2 of the 2026 World Series has ended. Read below for a full recap of Saturday’s game and analysis from CNN Sports’ Hannah Keyser.

The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 to take Game 2 of the World Series on Saturday at American Family Field.

Saturday’s game proved to be a bit more complex for the Brew Crew, having to erase an early huge deficit to go up 2-0 in the best-of-seven series.

The Rays jumped on Milwaukee’s rookie sensation Logan Henderson, scoring four runs in the first inning, highlighted by Liam Hicks’ two-run home run.

But as the Brewers have proved all season, an early hole doesn’t affect them in the slightest.

Milwaukee clawed back in the bottom of the first, adding two runs to make it a 4-2 game.

After a shaky start to the game, both starting pitchers — Henderson and Drew Rasmussen found their grove until the bottom of the fourth inning when Rays first baseman Jonathan Aranda’s error at first allowed the Brewers to make it a one-run game.

Both teams turned to their respective bullpens, but the tide truly turned in the bottom of the sixth inning.

Rays’ relief pitcher Tyler Wells allowed a moonshot home run to Brewers’ outfielder Sal Frelick to tie the game at 4-4.

With the sold-out Milwaukee faithful behind them, they quickly took the lead the next inning with Cooper Pratt RBI single.

Brewers reliever Aaron Ashby has proved to be a workhorse for the team all postseason and after getting out of the eighth inning with ease, his ninth inning lift was a bit harder.

A leadoff double by Jonny DeLuca put the tying run in scoring position right away. However, the 28-year-old struck out Victor Mesa Jr, made pinch hitter Kevin Williamson ground out and struck out Yandy Diaz on a controversial check swing.

The Brewers clawed back from four runs down and yet again proved why this team loves playing from behind.

They improved 41-37 when allowing the first run this season, including the postseason and find themselves two games from bringing home the franchise’s first World Series title.

This is supposed to be analysis, but it just feels like the Brewers’ year.

OK, some caveats: A sold-out ballpark full of fans willing to pay obscene prices to see their hometown team finally back in the World Series will, indeed, give games a certain aura. Especially if they win. It’s like what a soundtrack does for a movie scene: Subconsciously tell you how to feel.

And the sound of 40,000-plus Midwesterners losing their minds did a lot over the past two nights to make the Brewers seem like the main characters in this World Series.

Recency bias factors, too. We forget how a team can set a home run record one night and get literally no-hit the next (see the Phillies in the World Series in 2022). The Brewers have enjoyed their home field advantage this weekend and the Rays may do the same when the series turns to Tropicana Field on Monday.

But it’s not just the W that makes Milwaukee feel inevitable. After the Rays jumped out to a 4-0 lead in the first, we highlighted an utterly absurd statistic. This year the Brewers have a better than .500 after falling behind .

The best team in baseball got that way by beating the other team more often than not when they’re up, and when they’re down. Combined with the best bullpen in the National League and the games go a little something like this: They always have a good chance to come back, but the opposition does not.

Destiny, though, requires more than just dominating stats. It requires the ball bouncing your way and an unexpected hero coming through in a big moment.

He was, perhaps, the least likely member of the Brewers lineup to hit a 408-foot home run to straightaway center off a lefty reliever. And so of course that’s exactly what he did, to tie the game and complete the comeback.

Some home runs have their importance underscored by the author taking his time to admire his moon shot and round the base paths, milking every moment. But Frelick scampered out of the box and sped around the bases like he was eager to keep the momentum moving.

The next inning, rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt smacked the go-ahead single. It was his error in the first that had kicked off the Rays’ four-run frame and then there he was: the living embodiment of the Brewers overcoming early failures for ultimate victory.

It’s a potent fallback to winning easily.

Of course, twice now the Rays have ended the game with the tying run on third base – which you a testament to just how well-matched these two teams are. Or could draw your attention to how Tampa has gone 3-20 with runners in scoring position through the first two games of this Fall Classic.

It’s one of the toughest judgment calls in sports: When does a hitter go too far on a checked swing?

Yandy Díaz clearly thought he held up in time and Aaron Ashby’s curveball should have been ball four. There are 40,000-some-odd folks at American Family Field who will say this was a clear swing and Díaz went too far.

The longtime Ray had to be restrained after the game and guided off the field by coaches and teammates. It’s a really close call – I’m honestly not sure what I think!

You be the judge – should this have been strike three?

Once again, the Rays were not going to go quietly.

Jonny DeLuca started off the inning with a double down the right field line, putting the tying run in scoring position with no outs on the board. It was a near repeat of Friday’s night Game 1 when the Rays rallied in the top of the ninth to make things close as the Brewers tried to seal the win.

Victor Mesa Jr. followed that up with a strike out and some nifty work behind the plate from William Contreras kept DeLuca from advancing on balls in the dirt. Ben Williamson pinch hit for Taylor Walls and Aaron Ashby got him to ground out to second, moving DeLuca over to third.

Yandy Díaz stepped to the plate and worked a full count. With American Family Field rocking, Ashby reared back and threw a nasty curve that Díaz tried to hold up on.

The first base ump ruled he went too far and called strike three, putting a ninth inning Tampa rally to bed for a second straight night.

Milwaukee now has a commanding 2-0 lead in this best-of-seven World Series!

Buckle in folks, the ninth inning in upon us.

The Brewers had runners on second and third twice in the bottom of the eighth inning and both times came up just short in adding runs.

Jackson Chourio was tagged out after trying to score from third on a ground ball with the infield in, a play that was challenged and upheld. There was a pitching change on top of the review, so that half inning sort of dragged.

Anyways, Aaron Ashby is staying out to try to close things out.

Tampa has now gone seven innings since they last plated a run and in that time the Brewers have come all the way back to tie it, take the lead and turn the game over to their best bullpen arms.

Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby combine for a 1-2-3 inning and the Rays are running out of game.Great bullpens shorten games – meaning they make the last few frames essentially meaningless for the opposition – and you’re seeing that in action.

The Rays threatened earlier and failed to capitalize and now they’re facing the highest-leverage arms.

Cooper Pratt hasn’t had the best defensive showing in the first two games but maybe he can be forgiven after singling in the go-ahead run in the bottom of the seventh inning.

Brice Turang got the inning off with a bang, smacking a double to center field to put him into scoring position quickly.

Garrett Mitchell followed it up with a long sacrifice fly to move Turang to third.

The Brewers wanted to add more in the rest of the bottom of the seventh, but ultimately couldn’t get Pratt in – even though Sal Frelick thought he had another home run that fell just short of the wall.

Another inning, another base runner stranded for the Rays.

This time it’s Taylor Walls, the nine-hole hitter, who works a walk to lead off the frame – an auspicious start for the Rays. He gets all the way to third base with aggressive speed, but that’s as far as he makes it.

Not to pick on Yandy Díaz, but the DH led the American League in hits this regular season and through most of two games he is hitless, with an uncharacteristic pair of Ks tonight.

In a pregame post, I used Brewers manager Pat Murphy’s flattering comps for Sal Frelick – Joe Montana, Larry Bird – as evidence of the skipper’s tendency to use hyperbole.

But Murph knows his guys – and Frelick, especially, is his guy. They have what Frelick called a “unique relationship.”

“He likes to get after me pretty much 24/7,” Frelick said earlier this week. (“I don’t speak to the kid,” Murphy joked.)

But the razzing, of course, is borne of affection.

“I had a cool moment with him after Game 4 in LA, just embracing him,” Frelick said. “I know how much it means to him, how much he loves us.”

Before Game 2, Murphy described Frelick as the kind of player whose value defies analytics.

“I can’t tell you why Sal is just a little bit better than what anybody would rate him as,” he said. “I can describe it, but you can’t measure it.”

On the biggest stage, with the Brewers looking to battle back from an early four-run deficit, Frelick came through – his first home run of the postseason and just his fourth career homer off a left-handed pitcher – to tie it.

The 26-year-old outfielder hit a moonshot solo home run to center field to tie it up at 4-4.

With the crowd behind them, the Brewers threatened to tack on more after Chandler Simpson dropped a routine fly ball to potentially end the inning.

The mistake led to William Contreras coming to the plate but relief pitcher Tyler Wells was able to get him to ground out.

Out of 567 players whose sprint speeds were tracked by Statcast this season, Rays catcher Liam Hicks clocked in at number 501, traveling 25.7 feet per second. (For comparison, his speed-specialist teammate Chandler Simpson scampers around the basepaths at 29.4 feet per second).

That’s a pretty good reason to have not sent Hicks home on a ball hit to the left fielder Jackson Chourio, a literal Gold Glove finalist this year. And, indeed, the aggressive send backfires.

Hicks is thrown out at the plate for the final out of the frame. The Rays have put traffic on the bases all night but haven’t scored for five innings now.

The Milwaukee Brewers are deadly serious about their baseball this season.

Finishing with the best record in MLB, they’re hoping that this will be the year they can finally win a World Series after clinching a spot in the Fall Classic. But this is a franchise that doesn’t always take itself too seriously, and the bright lights of October will help showcase one of the most wonderfully ridiculous servings in sport: The slapstick sixth-inning sausage race.

It’s exactly as absurd as it sounds. Human runners, wearing 7-foot-tall foam costumes with goofy faces and colorful features depicting a Bratwurst, Polish, Italian, Hot Dog and Chorizo, race each other around home plate on the warning track. The comedically top-heavy sausages, which can easily topple forwards into the dirt, temporarily take center stage as the baseball players gaze on in amusement from their dugouts, sometimes wagering on the outcome.

Relief pitcher Cam Booser probably owes outfielder Victor Mesa Jr. lunch when they get back to Florida.

William Contreras has been unstoppable this postseason but Mesa made a sliding catch look easy, robbing the star catcher of his third hit of the game.

Despite a walk to Cooper Pratt, Booser was able to get out of the fifth inning with relative ease.

Rays shortstop Taylor Walls spoke pregame about Mesa’s defensive capabilities.

A section of seats on the first level just towards the third-base side of home plate seems to be the Rays’ family and friends section.

They’ve been counter-cheering all night, managing coordinated encouragement for each Tampa hitter. They haven’t had a whole lot to get excited about since the first inning.

A double by Jonathan Aranda – an admirable feat of not taking his costly error with him, mentally, to the plate – gets them going briefly in the fifth. But he’s ultimately stranded at third in Brewers’ long reliever Dustin May’s first frame.

The rhythm Drew Rasmussen found after the first inning is gone and so is he – but it wasn’t all his fault.

After getting Garrett Mitchell to ground out, he followed it up with walking Cooper Pratt and allowing a Sal Frelick single.

With runners on first and third, Rasmussen appeared to have maybe cooked up a double play ball, but it went through first baseman Jonathan Aranda’s glove, allowing Pratt to score.

The bleeding didn’t stop there as Rasmussen walked Jake Bauers, triggering a pitching change with the bases loaded.

Relief pitcher Cam Booser came in, threw two pitches and got Christian Yelich to ground out to second, escaping with limited damage.

Milwaukee turned to their bullpen for the fourth and JoJo Romero turned in a clean frame.

Jonny DeLuca managed a single on a ball that Statcast measured at traveling just two feet in front of home plate, but he didn’t get past first.

After fireworks in the first, this game has seriously slowed down on the action front.

Drew Rasmussen has arrived in Milwaukee. The first inning was just a fluke.

After quickly striking out Jake Bauers and Christian Yelich, Rasmussen found some issues with William Contreras (who, by the way, is batting almost .400 this postseason).

But that single turned out to be a nothing burger as Rasmussen got Brice Turang to ground out to end the inning.

It remains a two-run game heading into the fourth inning.

Here’s the kind of boots-on-the-ground reporting I came to Milwaukee to be able to provide to this live story.

I was initially disappointed in the lack of a giant celebratory sheetcake in the press box. In previous postseason I’ve covered, there is a giant cake with the World Series logo on it (or, sometimes: cupcakes, cookies, other sweets festooned with sugary food dye.)

However, I would like to make it known that Milwaukee is providing in other ways. This is, perhaps, the best press box soft serve ice cream I’ve had anywhere in baseball. Only quibble – maybe have some sprinkles?

Also, the Rays went down 1-2-3 in the third inning.

Can you believe there were no runs scored in the second inning by any team?

The Brewers, still down two runs, went down 1-2-3 without much fight as Rays ace Drew Rasmussen has appeared to find his footing in this contest.

Remember, Rasmussen has yet to give up more than two runs in any start since mid-August.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 8 Early Waiver Wire Pickups: Caleb Douglas, Kaelon Black among top options
articles.summary: We go over some early waiver wire options for your fantasy football lineups in Week 8.
articles.body:
It's about the midway point of the fantasy football season. How are your lineups looking so far? If they still need some work or you need an injury fill-in, you'll need to look to the waiver wire. We also have four teams on bye in Week 8 with the 49ers, Giants, Saints and Texans out of action, so keep that in mind. Below, we're going over some early waiver wire options coming out of Sunday's games.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins (9% rostered on Yahoo)

Miami came out of the bye looking for its first win of the season on Sunday. The Dolphins went on the road and were able to upset the Jets thanks to a big performance from the rookie wide receiver out of Texas Tech. After bursting onto the scene with a 5-94-0 line, an ankle injury would keep Douglas out for most of the next four games prior to the Week 6 bye. He shook off the injury to return on Sunday, scoring on each of his two catches (one a 63-yarder, the other a seven-yard score) for 20 fantasy points.

The big play made up most of Douglas' fantasy production but we saw proof of concept in Week 1 as well. The Dolphins figure to be trailing plenty in games the rest of the season. That bodes well for Douglas being needed in the passing game for chunk plays. Like we saw last week with Omar Cooper Jr. (more on him below), Douglas is a great upside pickup or potentially a solid plug-and-play in Week 8 if you need a WR in a deeper league.

Omar Cooper Jr., WR, Jets (47% rostered)

Speaking of Cooper and proof of concept, here's another rookie wideout who is clearly legit. All Cooper did in that Jets-Dolphins game was follow up his breakout performance with a slightly better stat line of 5-115-1 to get to 20 fantasy points after posting 19.3 last week. What's surprising about this performance from Cooper is the fact WR Adonai Mitchell, the previous WR2 for the Jets, was back in the fold after an extended absence. Mitchell was held without a catch on three targets against Miami.

Now, we shouldn't expect this every week from Cooper but this is what his ceiling could be in fantasy. He should settle into a solid role the rest of the season and the Jets should be in positive scripts for passing most games. More defenses could key in on Garrett Wilson and the run game, which would be even better for Coop. He's looking like a solid WR2/3 option moving forward.

This is likely the last call on Cooper; don't expect him to be available in many leagues by Wednesday.

The 49ers are dealing with injuries in the receiver ranks to Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. Fans collectively held their breath when Christian McCaffrey left on Sunday against the Falcons, though he was able to get back on the field. But with a lack of receiving options, the run game became a priority this week. And to preserve CMC, Kyle Shanahan turned to the rookie back.

Black led the ground game with 12 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown for 10.4 fantasy points. The Niners will always favor McCaffrey in the passing game but Black could take on more of the rushing work. If Black is hanging around on your waiver wire, grab him. He's becoming a decent flex play on top of being the best "next man up" in fantasy football.

articles.title: How PV Sindhu came  close but failed to end decade of frustration against An Se Young
articles.summary: PV Sindhu came agonisingly close to ending a decade of frustration against An Se Young. But the World No.
articles.body: PV Sindhu came agonisingly close to ending a decade of frustration against An Se Young. But the World No. 1 from South Korea, unbeaten against the Indian in 11 meetings now, found another gear when it mattered, storming back to win the French Open BWF Super 750 final 16-21, 21-11, 21-12 on Sunday.The top seed’s latest triumph was historic in more ways than one. It was her 10th title of the 2026 season, her fourth French Open crown overall and her third in a row. It also stretched her unbroken winning run to 50 matches, a measure of the dominance she has built in women’s singles.For a large part of the opening game, the script appeared to be heading in an unfamiliar direction. Sindhu came out aggressively, attacking from the first rally and pushing An onto the back foot with a barrage of sharp smashes to stretch the advantage to 15-9. She stayed composed in the closing stages, reached game point and completed the 21-16 win.By An’s own admission, she was rushing and could not find the length in that game.The champion’s response in the second game was swift and emphatic. She raced to a 3-0 lead and soon made it 11-7. The lead ballooned to 19-8 before she sealed the game 21-11 and levelled the match.Once An found her range, she was dominant. Her movement, especially from the backcourt to the net, was lightning quick, and she toyed with the Indian through an array of shots.The third game began in Sindhu’s favour. She moved to a 3-1 lead, only for An to regain control and edge ahead at 5-4. The Indian continued to fight and opened up an 8-5 advantage while An briefly struggled to find her rhythm.That was the moment the match could have tilted. But An, exploiting gaps in Sindhu’s movement, fought back to level at 8-8 and then took an 11-9 lead into the interval. From there she tightened her grip, mixing delicate net shots and pushes with powerful smashes to stretch the advantage to 15-9. She completed the 21-12 win.Sindhu left the court disappointed but encouraged by her performance, particularly after taking a game off the World No. 1.“I fought for every point, I could win the first game and I was happy about it,” she said.Pointing to the decider, she added: “Even in the third set, I should have maintained the lead from 8-5. But unfortunate that she converted that into 11-9. So that’s where I felt the difference was. But a lot of positives to take from this match. Going forward, I need to work on them.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I feel proud of myself': Basketball player Pushpa Senthil Kumar's journey from learning to leading
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Nearly a decade ago, Pushpa Senthil Kumar stood at the Sree Kanteerava Indoor Stadium here, grappling with the nerves of captaining an Indian
articles.body: BENGALURU: Nearly a decade ago, Pushpa Senthil Kumar stood at the Sree Kanteerava Indoor Stadium here, grappling with the nerves of captaining an Indian team for the first time. On her return to the same venue, she was no longer the uncertain teenager seeking guidance, but a 25-year-old leading Indian Railways against Asia’s best. The results were disappointing, with her team losing all three matches in the FIBA Women’s Basketball League Asia, but the return offered a moment to reflect on how far she had come.She had represented India at the U-16 level at the venue in 2017 and remembers the nervousness of captaining a team at that age, as well as the support she received from coach Zoran Visic. He helped her navigate an environment where communicating with teammates and coaches was challenging, and now she is a more confident skipper.“I feel proud of myself because the coaches believed in me. I was young and nervous back then. But my coach always backed me and turned me into a confident player and leader. And now, I am more experienced, and I trust my players and give them confidence. When we are low and feel like giving up, I support my teammates,” she told TOI.That confidence was hard-earned. Growing up in Mudikandanallur, a village in Tamil Nadu’s Nagapattinam district, Pushpa initially took up netball at a Sports Authority of India hostel in Mayiladuthurai, alongside her elder sister Sathiya. When netball opportunities dwindled, she turned to basketball. What began as a change of sport eventually led to a career and a place on the national team.Her international career began at the 2017 U-16 Women’s Asia Championship Division B, where she averaged 13.2 points and 13.2 rebounds. She moved to the U-18 team the following year and then made her senior debut at the 2021 Women’s Asia Cup Division A. At the 2025 Asia Cup Division B, she averaged 14.2 points and 6.6 rebounds, establishing herself as one of India’s key players.Off the court, sport also brought financial stability to her family. After her father’s death, her mother worked in a garment factory to support her daughters. Pushpa secured a Railways job in 2019.“I told my mother that I would take care of her because of our family situation, and the sport and Railways have helped me fulfil my responsibilities,” she added.As captain of a young team, Pushpa is equally conscious of the responsibility she carries. Seeing many youngsters come in, she wants the next generation to approach the game with greater belief and determination. “We have to focus and believe in ourselves,” she said.Her ambition is straightforward: to see India win more often. She believes the defeats in Bengaluru should serve as lessons, not setbacks, and adds, “I want us to win more. Women’s basketball has been going down, and we have to improve.”For a player who once arrived at the venue unsure how to lead, the journey has shown growth, responsibility, and belief, leaving her determined to help India win more often and turn lessons into results.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: D Gukesh vs Javokhir Sindarov: What do world's top GMs think about the upcoming World Chess Championship match?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A pressure cooker may seem like a less flamboyant invention these days, especially with Elon Musk’s “flying cars” making the rounds on the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A pressure cooker may seem like a less flamboyant invention these days, especially with Elon Musk’s “flying cars” making the rounds on the internet. Yet, it remains a fascinating feat of human-led engineering, built on a simple principle of physics. Seal the vessel, trap the heat, and raise the internal pressure to allow temperatures that ordinary atmospheric conditions would not permit.In sports, defending a world title can have a similar effect on the human mind, can't it?When you are chasing a championship, every win feels like free money. But once the lid seals and you’re holding the crown, every draw feels like a defense, every loss feels like a crisis, and the pressure cooker turns on.That psychological pressure cooker is the backdrop for next month’s World Championship match in Geneva.India's Dommaraju Gukesh is that young champion struggling to rediscover his peak form. Meanwhile, 20-year-old Javokhir Sindarov enters with maximum momentum after tearing through the Candidates Tournament in Cyprus.Outwardly, it looks like a battle between a confident challenger and a champion under siege. But is there more to it? With less than a month remaining for the mega encounter, TimesofIndia.com today looks at what the world’s top grandmasters think about the 14-game duel ahead.'Sometimes it all comes down to one move': Nepo"They always say that match is very different to normal tournaments and that's true," former World Championship challenger and current Russian No. 1 Ian Nepomniachtchi told this website. "But if we see Gukesh's progress for the past like couple of years I believe is pretty much negative. I don't know what happened to him, honestly. And as for now, I think Sindarov is of course a clear favourite."Nepomniachtchi feels that Gukesh’s last truly commanding performance was at Wijk aan Zee in early 2025, where he finished tied for first with fellow Indian Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa but lost the title on tiebreak. After that, it has been abysmal.Nevertheless, Nepo, now 36, also knows firsthand how quickly a match dynamic can shift once the clocks start ticking."Once again, the match is very special, and if you manage to clinch one win (at the start), then you can sit behind your opening prep," Nepomniachtchi added."I think a good example is the Karjakin-Carlsen match. So no one expected Sergey to be like such a tough opponent for Magnus. But I think Sergey had a very, very fair chance to win... Sometimes it all comes down to one move."'I expect Gukesh to be in a fighting mood': AronianThat psychological weight of wearing the champion's armour so early in life is something veteran grandmaster Levon Aronian views with deep empathy."Gukesh is a big fighter," Aronian said in an interaction with TimesofIndia.com. "He has been a bit down, but I expect him to be in a fighting mood for the match. Of course, it's tremendous pressure. You know, you're so young and your lifetime dream just came too early. I think the same kind of thing happened to Mikhail Tal. He also became a world champion too early. And of course, it's normal to be overwhelmed."At the moment, people think that Gukesh is going to go and try to be very cautious, like in a similar style to how Ding (Liren) was doing against Nepomniachtchi, or also the way Ding was playing against Gukesh as well," Aronian remarked. "There are so many choices to make, and it's definitely going to be an interesting match from a strategical point. I expect Sindarov to be continuing playing very interesting chess the way he's doing."'Chess is a highly psychological game': CarlsenWhile Sindarov arrives with wind in his sails, five-time World Champion Magnus Carlsen believes the framing around Gukesh’s mindset needs a complete reset."The word 'defend' is really not a good place to begin, because in terms of how Gukesh has played for the last couple of years, he should not be in a position where he has to defend anything," Carlsen, when asked about Gukesh's chances of defending the World Championship crown, explained. "He should be in a position where he has everything to gain."Emphasising that classical matches are deeply psychological, Carlsen also feels a single shift in momentum can completely rewrite expectations."He (Gukesh) has shown previously in 2024 that when things click, he has the potential to play at an extremely high level," the current World No. 1 added. "I don't think a lot of people believe that he will do it now, but I think it's even more of an interesting challenge for him to try and get back to that. Chess is a highly psychological game, so it probably won't take a lot to potentially place some doubts in Sindarov's mind and some confidence for Gukesh."'Gukesh needs to arrive with a positive mindset': MVLCarlsen's sentiment was echoed by French grandmaster Maxime Vachier-Lagrave, who senses that while Sindarov brings stability and form, Gukesh holds the key to how the match actually unfolds."From Sindarov’s point of view, I think it’s clear that this year he has been quite successful," MVL told TimesofIndia.com. "He has been very clutch, very calm, and very determined. So, he is not the variable. Gukesh is the variable."Fresh off the Chess Olympiad, where Gukesh won two silver medals, 36-year-old MVL believes the Samarkand experience could well turn the tide for the Indian grandmaster."I think, of course, all the talk is about how Gukesh has been struggling over the past few months," MVL remarked. "And I do think he needs to arrive with a positive mindset because, chess-wise, if he plays at his best level, he is at least as good as Sindarov. Gukesh has been playing extremely well in the past two Olympiads. If he can use that to play well again, maybe this will be the way for him to get into a positive mindset before the match."'Gukesh has enough time to regain his form': Wei YiChina's top-ranked player, Wei Yi, who competed alongside Sindarov in Cyprus, cautioned against writing off the reigning champion based purely on recent rating points."Yes, I also participated in the Candidates Tournament in Cyprus earlier this year," Wei told TimesofIndia.com."We all know that Sindarov ultimately won the tournament. He performed extremely well and secured first place with a commanding lead, clinching the title ahead of the final round. However, some people may feel that Gukesh has not been in particularly good form recently, and his rating has been declining. If he continues in this form, they might expect the World Championship match to be one-sided, with Sindarov winning comfortably. But I don't think it will be that simple, because there is still time before the match. I believe Gukesh has enough time to regain his form, and I'm sure he has already started preparing."Wei pointed to a crucial factor that rating algorithms often miss."I believe experience will be extremely important in a contest like this," Wei added. "The World Championship match is different from any other tournament. Two players are fighting for the highest title in chess, and they have to face the same opponent over nearly a month, constantly thinking about how to defeat them. I think experience will certainly matter, and Gukesh clearly has an advantage in that respect."'A real battle of minds between the two players'Giving an update on Gukesh's mentality after this Olympiad, GM Srinath Narayanan, who captained the Indian team in the open section at this 2026 Samarkand Olympiad, agreed that the unique format of match play acts as a great equaliser."I think Gukesh is in a much better mental space after the Olympiad, because it was probably his first really good tournament in a long time," Srinath told this website. "It will be close, not as one-sided as what the ratings reflect. Javokhir enters with a lot of confidence, and that can change if there's an early good result for Gukesh."Srinath noted that while Sindarov's opening preparation has looked formidable in recent months, but it will not matter much when he sits in Geneva later next month."He's also showing an incredible amount of opening preparation against other opponents, but in a World Championship match, this gets neutralised," Srinath remarked. "Both players see everything the other has. There are factors going Javokhir's way right now, but they can even out over a match. I think it's going to be a very close, very interesting one.""I think it will be a close match probably," Alireza Firouzja noted, keeping it short. "Anything could happen."If anything, Geneva will not merely test engine lines and endgame technique, as Wei Yi concluded, "Personally, it will be a very close match. I can't say for certain who will win, but regardless of who I think might win or who I want to win, I hope we get to see a fantastic contest, a real battle of minds between the two players."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dakar Rally 2027 moved out of Saudi Arabia amid conflict in Middle East
articles.summary: Organisers of January’s off-road race say it will be relocated due to recent developments in the region.
articles.body:
The Dakar Rally, one of the world’s toughest and best-known off-road races, has been moved out of Saudi Arabia for the 2027 edition due to the “recent developments in the region”, organisers say.

The rally, scheduled for January, will now be held “in a different territory” to be announced later before a planned return to Saudi Arabia in 2028, the Amaury Sport Organisation and Saudi Motorsport Company said in a statement on Sunday.

A new location will be announced in the “coming days”, the statement added.

It’s the latest in a series of sports events to be moved out of Saudi Arabia this year over the US-Israel war on Iran and deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Arabia has hosted the Dakar Rally since 2020. Reports in specialist race media said a move to Morocco or Spain is being considered.

If it is moved to Morocco, it would be the first time the Dakar has been held in Africa since 2007. The event began as a competition from Paris to Senegal’s capital, Dakar. It was cancelled on short notice in 2008 over security concerns in North Africa. Since then, it has been held first in South America, then in Saudi Arabia.

Organisers said they intend to bring the rally back to Saudi Arabia in 2028 to celebrate its 50th edition.

This season’s Formula One grand prix in Jeddah was cancelled while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia.

The final round of the World Rally Championship in Saudi Arabia next month has also been scrapped.

An exhibition tennis tournament in Saudi Arabia due to feature Novak Djokovic, Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev has been postponed until late December.

The WTA Finals were also scheduled to be held in Riyadh next month but will instead take place at Indian Wells, California, in the United States.

The last two races of the F1 season in Qatar (November 29) and Abu Dhabi (December 6) are still on the calendar, as is the Qatar MotoGP next month, but they are the subject of intense internal debate.

Dakar Rally organisers had hoped to keep the 2027 race in Saudi Arabia by working on a new route in the northern part of the country.

But the latest strikes, including a series of attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, which killed 18 people and injured hundreds more, have rendered that impossible.

Fighting between government forces and Houthi fighters has intensified across multiple fronts in Yemen in recent weeks, causing a spiralling humanitarian crisis .

The war in Yemen escalated sharply when the Houthis seized strategic territory from forces loyal to the country’s internationally recognised government along the Red Sea coast last month.

The Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition supporting Yemen’s government forces, have dealt a huge blow to the kingdom, the world’s biggest exporter of crude oil, disrupting its businesses, airlines and normal life and damaging its international image.

articles.title: Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers gushes over Paris, but there was 1 thing he knows he ‘screwed up’
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers had plenty of reasons to celebrate his Paris experience after guiding the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints. Howe...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers had plenty of reasons to celebrate his Paris experience after guiding the Pittsburgh Steelers to a 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints . However, while the veteran quarterback enjoyed the historic occasion, he admitted that one unfamiliar aspect of the stadium caught him off guard during the game.

During his postgame press conference in Paris, Rodgers revealed that reading the stadium clock from his position under center proved more difficult than he had expected.

"You'd look up at the clock from my vantage point under center, there were like eight different numbers," Rodgers said. "And you're like looking for the one that's actually counting down, at one point. I totally screwed that one up."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The matchup marked the NFL's first regular-season game in France. Beyond the on-field action, Rodgers was particularly impressed by the stadium, the quality of the grass and the pregame ceremonies.

"But what a great stadium this was. I felt like it's really cool to be a part of. I thought the [playing] surface was good, the grass. I thought the environment was great. And just all the pomp and circumstance before, you know. I thought the French anthem was, I thought, just so gorgeous, I mean, just really beautiful. And to hear the fans sing along, too, was a really cool moment, I thought."

While Rodgers appreciated the atmosphere in Paris, the Steelers still had to put together a strong performance to secure the victory. The veteran quarterback completed 19 of his 30 passing attempts for 212 yards and one touchdown. He finished the game without throwing an interception.

Running back Jaylen Warren also played a crucial role in the Steelers' success, recording 101 rushing yards on 18 carries.

The victory improved the Steelers' record to 5-2, keeping them at the top of their division. Rodgers and his teammates will now turn their attention to a rematch against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday at Acrisure Stadium.

articles.title: “We wanted to win”: Eva Olid exemplifies incredible standards at Man United Women after City draw
articles.summary: Manchester United Women secured another fine result as Eva Olid’s side came from behind to draw 1-1 with Manchester City.The gameThe Red Devils were on a six...
articles.body:
Manchester United Women secured another fine result as Eva Olid's side came from behind to draw 1-1 with Manchester City.

The Red Devils were on a six-game winning streak but fell behind to Khadija Shaw's strike in the second half.

Nonetheless, United Women are nothing if not fighters and they came roaring back and scored an equaliser in the 89th minute through Elisabeth Terland.

The home side were well worth the point and played some brave, attacking football at times that could have resulted in more goals.

One such example was a stunning effort from Jess Park that crashed off the crossbar.

The Catalan coach has been fundamental to United's change in fortunes lately and spoke to the club's media after the match.

Explaining how she felt the match unfolded, she stated, "in possession, I think we controlled the game more than them, we had more possession than them. They were more counter attacking and playing direct balls into the space, and it's how they were trying to hurt us, and we were hurting them trying to build from the back and trying to be ourselves."

There was tension between Manchester United captain Maya Le Tissier and Shaw but Olid played down the incident.

She asserted, "both are competitive and we know that she's one of the best strikers in the league, and we know that sometimes she can be frustrated if she's not having the ball. Of course we plan to mark her, be close to her so she can feel the pressing, but still she has one ball in the box and she scores, that is what top players do."

Olid also added that her team deserved the win but they just need to find a way of putting the ball into the back of the net more often.

Asked what she can do about the situation, she claimed, "for me as a manager what I can do is help the team the whole week for when we have the chances and the opportunities to score. It's training, training, practice, practice, practice, and keep growing in front of the goal. Next time, instead of scoring one, we can score more goals."

Commenting on her reaction to the match, she said, "we wanted to win and I think we showed today that we really wanted to win this game, and I never say this, but today we really deserved to win, and now it's a mix of feelings. But football sometimes is unfair."

Manchester United will next be in action at home to Burnley on Wednesday night in the Players' Cup.

articles.title: Auburn's Defensive Struggles Against LSU Raise Serious Questions for DJ Durkin
articles.summary: Auburn's secondary struggled in a 38-17 loss to LSU, allowing Sam Leavitt to throw for 387 yards. With Andre Jordan Jr. struggling in coverage and AnQuon Feg...
articles.body:
The Auburn Tigers defense had arguably its worst performance of the season in Saturday's 38-17 loss to LSU at Jordan-Hare Stadium.

They allowed 552 total yards, including 387 through the air, as Sam Leavitt and the LSU offense had their way with Auburn's secondary. But one of the biggest questions coming out of the loss is why Auburn didn't make more personnel adjustments defensively.

Especially considering how the coaching staff handled mistakes on the offensive side of the football.

Auburn's secondary struggled all afternoon.

LSU wide receiver Jackson Harris finished with nine receptions for 178 yards and two touchdowns.

Andre Jordan Jr. had a difficult afternoon in coverage, while the Tigers also struggled with assignments and tackling in the secondary. After being successful, especially as a boundary defender against Georgia a week ago, he struggled mightily against LSU. He allowed 10 receptions on 10 targets, 100% of the passes thrown his way were caught by LSU receivers, for a total of 114 yards.

One of the biggest plays came after Auburn safety Eric Winters left the game with an injury.

AnQuon Fegans entered the contest and missed his coverage assignment as the helping safety, allowing Harris to score on a 70-yard touchdown reception.

And while mistakes are going to happen, Auburn continued to struggle without finding an answer.

That's where some questions about the coaching staff come into play.

Auburn has other defensive backs on its roster, including Gavin Jenkins, who earlier this offseason Alex Golesh stated is an NFL-caliber corner. However, he isn't getting any reps.

Yet the Tigers continued relying on the same players while LSU consistently found success throwing the football. The fact they didn't at least try different combinations, even when the game was out of reach is certainly head scratching.

And that's interesting considering what happened with Auburn running back Jeremiah Cobb.

Cobb reportedly missed a blitz pickup during the contest and was subsequently held out for three consecutive offensive series.

That's a significant consequence for one mistake.

But on the defensive side of the football, Auburn had players repeatedly struggling in coverage without seeing similar changes. There's certainly a difference between missing an assignment and simply getting beaten by a talented opponent.

When LSU is consistently finding open receivers, shouldn't Auburn at least consider trying something different?

Auburn's defensive coordinator has now watched his unit struggle against multiple SEC opponents this season.

And Saturday was arguably the most concerning performance yet.

The Tigers couldn't consistently pressure Leavitt, struggled to tackle in open space, and allowed too many explosive plays.

Auburn has shown that it can compete with some of the best teams in college football.

But the loss to LSU showed that the coaching staff still has plenty to figure out.

And that includes knowing when it's time to make a change.

articles.title: Texas Senator Ted Cruz’s appearance at United States GP podium ceremony leads to loud boos from fans
articles.summary: Texas Senator and Chief of the Senate Commerce Committee Ted Cruz appeared on the podium for Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix in Austin. Cruz has been an...
articles.body:
Texas Senator and Chief of the Senate Commerce Committee Ted Cruz appeared on the podium for Formula 1's United States Grand Prix in Austin.

Cruz has been an elected member of the United States Senate from Texas since 2013, but likely did not get the reception he expected when he appeared on the podium to hand out the trophies to the top-three drivers at the 2026 U.S. GP.

As Cruz handed trophies to Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc, and Kimi Antonelli, the crowd at Austin let their feelings on their elected Senator know.

Ted Cruz receives heavy boos at Formula 1 appearance in Texas

As Cruz appeared on the F1 podium stage, the crowd very audibly started booing, even continuing the boos when race-winner Antonelli lifted up the trophy handed to him by Cruz. F1 commentator James Crofty acknowledged the boos on the broadcast as well.

"People are already voting with their voice."

Cruz is not up for election in 2026, but has endorsed Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton in his race against the Democratic nominee James Talarico.

The last election Cruz ran in was the 2024 race for the Class I Senate seat in Texas, winning over Democratic nominee Colin Alfred.

Notably, Austin, where the 2026 United States GP was held, gave 70% of its votes to Alfred in that race, with Cruz receiving just 27.16% of the popular vote in the city. He has previously been unpopular in Austin, so it should not be surprising to see the fans here react this way to Cruz.

Cruz's appearance at the 2026 U.S. GP is not a rare occurrence for an American politician. Most notably, Donald Trump attended the 2024 Miami Grand Prix, albeit before winning the 2024 U.S. Presidential election.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has attended multiple Miami Grand Prix events since the race's addition to the F1 calendar in 2024. Texas Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick also attended the U.S. GP in Austin.

articles.title: Michael Carrick says waving to fans after Bournemouth thrashing ‘wasn’t a farewell’
articles.summary: Head coach Michael Carrick was still serenaded by supportive fans inside Old Trafford but conceded he was unsure if he would keep his job
articles.body:
Michael Carrick insisted he was not saying farewell to Manchester United after their 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth but admitted he does not know if he will be sacked.

United have made their worst start to a season for 40 years and lost their last two games by three goals, following Wednesday's 4-1 thrashing by Como , and Carrick was taunted by Bournemouth supporters with chants of "sacked in the morning".

He was still serenaded by United fans as he went down the tunnel but claimed: "It wasn't a farewell from me."

He said he had only had a short conversation after the game with the United hierarchy and is not sure if chief executive Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox will dismiss him.

"Just briefly like always after a game, but nothing out of the ordinary," he added. "I will see what happens. I totally understand the situation.

"I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I am carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, whatever decision is made on anything really. So that's kind of it. You know, I'm not expecting anything either way."

Carrick insisted the United players are hurting as their nosedive continues but admitted he has not spoken to them all.

"There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of disappointment, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, disappointed," he said.

"It's not like they don't care, or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to - I've not spoke to everyone individually, the ones I have spoken to, it's affecting them a lot."

Carrick said he was left with a variety of feelings as he thanked the United fans for their backing. "Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way," he said. "To feel the connection and appreciation from the supporters, I feel it and appreciate it a lot."

articles.title: Celtic Confirm More Bad News After Hibernian Game
articles.summary: Celtic have more injury problems on their hands coming out of the game against Hibernian.
articles.body:
Many Celtic fans would have been viewing the game against Hibernian as a chance to get things back on track for the Hoops after their defeat at the hands of Celta Vigo in midweek. And although Martin O'Neill's side did win at Easter Road, it was not the confidence booster they would have been looking for.

An own goal from Hibernian and a strike from Camilo Duran secured a 2-1 win for Celtic at the weekend against a team sitting at the bottom of the Scottish Premiership table.

While O'Neill seemed content with the result coming out of the game, even happy, the same cannot be said about a lot of supporters.

And it is not just the result they need to be worried about. The club have been handed fresh injury concerns as well.

Alistair Johnston is someone who has faced constant injury problems over his time at Celtic. Unfortunately, things don't seem to be getting any better for the Canadian international.

Johnston was only making a return from injury in the game against Hibernian, coming on as a substitute. But he lasted only 20 minutes on the pitch before he had to be taken off again.

As reported by beIN Sports , O'Neill said regarding Johnston's injury coming out of the game:

"Alistair's felt something again, a little bit high up in his hamstring. A bit concerned about it. We don't know. We'll have to see.

"That would be a blow if he's out. You never know. It might be cramp. It might be a number of things.

"But he was really settling in brilliantly in the space of time that he was on the field."

Obviously, that is far from ideal. Was he rushed back from injury? Or is this a player who simply can't stay fit anymore?

On top of his game, Johnston is one of Celtic's best players. But due to his injury history, he is no longer someone the club can rely on.

If Celtic are convinced that Colby Donovan is their long-term starter then they probably should start settling him into that role moving forward. If not, they should look to bring in someone who can take up that spot.

As for Johnston, his time as a regular starter for Celtic might be as good as over. You simply cannot rely on a player who often spends more than half the season out injured. That is the unfortunate reality of the Canadian international's track record in recent times.

The best-case scenario for Celtic would be for Johnston to somehow recover his fitness to a level where he can play consistent football. But the signs do not point in that direction, unfortunately.

articles.title: Titans’ Robert Saleh refuses to admit he has a Cam Ward problem despite calling out bad misses
articles.summary: Cam Ward and Robert Saleh had a serious talk after the Tennessee Titans lost to the Houston Texans in Week 5, which kept them winless. It worked, as the Tita...
articles.body:
Cam Ward and Robert Saleh had a serious talk after the Tennessee Titans lost to the Houston Texans in Week 5, which kept them winless. It worked, as the Titans beat the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6 to end their losing skid.

Well, it looks like Ward and Saleh might need to have another chat.

The Titans bowed to the Cleveland Browns , 27-24, on Sunday, falling to 0-4 at Nissan Stadium. Ward went 20-of-31 for 181 yards, zero touchdowns, and one interception.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

While the second-year quarterback was subpar, Saleh stressed that their shortcomings against the Browns were "across the board," as reported by ESPN's Turron Davenport.

" Robert Saleh said there's blame to go around on offense. Saleh admitted Cam Ward should have made some throws he missed, but he doesn't think the offense has a quarterback problem," wrote Davenport.

The 24-year-old Ward, last year's No. 1 pick, could be in danger of losing his starting job in the coming weeks or being replaced next year if he fails to turn things around.

Saleh has been patient with the young signal-caller, but at some point, he might have to acknowledge that the Titans could be better off with a different leader.

The Titans struggled to limit the Browns' running attack, with Quinshon Judkins getting 17 carries for 96 yards and two touchdowns. Deshaun Watson, who threw 25-of-36 for 308 yards, scored on a nine-yard rush in the fourth quarter.

The defeat spoiled Tony Pollard's outstanding effort. He logged 25 carries for 129 yards and a career-high-tying three touchdowns.

Tennessee fell to 1-6, while Cleveland improved to 5-2.

articles.title: Jets must end Aaron Glenn era after rock-bottom loss to previously winless Dolphins
articles.summary: The New York Jets have officially run out of excuses. Losing to a struggling divisional rival is frustrating enough. However, allowing the previously winless...
articles.body:
The New York Jets have officially run out of excuses. Losing to a struggling divisional rival is frustrating enough. However, allowing the previously winless Miami Dolphins to leave MetLife Stadium with a 28-25 victory is nothing less than a damaging indictment of Aaron Glenn 's leadership. New York entered Week 7 with a chance to stabilize its season and build on a narrow victory over Cleveland. Instead, the Jets struggled to contain Miami's ground game and ultimately failed to complete a late comeback. At 2-5, New York's central question is becoming impossible to avoid: Is Glenn still the right person to lead this franchise?

New York's 2026 campaign has been defined by missed opportunities and inconsistent execution. The Jets opened with a victory over Tennessee before dropping three straight games against Green Bay, Detroit, and Chicago. A 17-12 win over Cleveland briefly offered relief. However, a 26-19 defeat to New England sent them into their Week 7 matchup at 2-4. Sunday's loss to Miami pushed them to 2-5, despite a spirited offensive response in the second half. Geno Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards and three touchdowns. Omar Cooper Jr. delivered 115 receiving yards. The Jets still fell short after allowing Miami to build a 21-7 halftime lead and produce 156 rushing yards. The Dolphins entered the game 0-5 and left with their first victory of the season.

New York's defense failed to impose its will against an offense that had struggled badly through the opening weeks. Miami quarterback Malik Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns. He repeatedly found ways to extend possessions. Running back Ollie Gordon II rushed for 103 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries. Miami converted all three of its fourth-down attempts, including a decisive quarterback sneak late in the fourth quarter that allowed it to drain the clock.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Those numbers tell a troubling story. New York could not consistently close running lanes or force Miami into the kind of mistakes that might have changed the game. The defense also failed to prevent a devastating 63-yard touchdown pass to Caleb Douglas late in the fourth quarter. That play restored Miami's two-score cushion just when the Jets were threatening to take control.

The late breakdowns were especially damaging because New York's offense had done enough to make the game competitive. A head coach must find a way to get his team prepared for precisely these situations. Glenn's defense repeatedly failed that test.

New York's roster has legitimate building blocks. Garrett Wilson remains a proven receiving threat . Breece Hall and Braelon Allen are dynamic running backs. The young receiving group has shown encouraging potential. Cooper's performance against Miami was another positive sign. Tight end Mason Taylor caught two touchdown passes.

Yet individual production has not translated into consistent winning football. The Jets have lost five of their first seven games. Their latest defeat came against a division opponent that had not won all season. This kind of result forces an organization to question whether its coaching staff is extracting enough from its personnel.

Glenn also faces questions about game management. Miami's 14-point halftime lead came after the Jets struggled to respond to the Dolphins' long possessions. New York had opportunities to limit the damage, but its defensive execution and late-half management left the team chasing the game.

Retaining Glenn simply because changing coaches is uncomfortable would be a questionable move forward. The franchise cannot afford to lose another season waiting for progress that has yet to materialize. The next few games should not become an indefinite extension of the same experiment.

New York should evaluate the coaching staff's performance honestly. They should start with its repeated struggles in high-leverage situations. If ownership believes Glenn cannot deliver meaningful improvement , making a change now would allow the organization to begin identifying the leadership it needs for 2027.

The Jets showed fight by scoring 18 points after halftime and pulling within three. Still, the comeback could not erase the failures that put them in that position. Miami converted a crucial fourth down, preserved possession, and secured its first win of the season.

Glenn deserves a fair assessment, but his record demands serious scrutiny. New York needs accountability, sharper preparation, and a coaching structure capable of turning its talent into victories.

At 2-5, the Jets still have a ton of games left to play. That said, the organization cannot keep pretending that patience alone will solve its problems. If Glenn cannot demonstrate that he can correct the defensive breakdowns and improve the team's situational execution, New York should end the experiment. The loss to Miami may be remembered as the moment the Jets finally recognized that another change was necessary.

articles.title: F1 Mexican GP 2026: All session times and full weekend schedule
articles.summary: Formula 1 heads to Mexico City for the Mexican Grand Prix, where Kimi Antonelli could take the final step towards his maiden World Championship. The Mercedes...
articles.body:
Formula 1 heads to Mexico City for the Mexican Grand Prix, where Kimi Antonelli could take the final step towards his maiden World Championship. The Mercedes driver arrives at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez with a genuine match point, following his first mathematical opportunity to seal the title at the United States Grand Prix in Austin.

The Italian youngster is approaching a potentially historic moment in his Formula 1 career. Although the championship mathematics already gave him an opportunity in Texas, Mexico presents another chance to settle the fight for the crown before the season reaches its final rounds.

The Mexican Grand Prix takes place from 30 October to 1 November, with the demanding Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez providing the backdrop for the weekend. Located at an altitude of more than 2,200 metres above sea level, the circuit presents unique challenges for teams, particularly in terms of cooling and aerodynamic performance.

What time is the 2026 Mexican Grand Prix?

As in Austin, Formula 1 will use its traditional weekend format in Mexico, with three practice sessions before Saturday's qualifying and Sunday's race.

The opening session gets underway on Friday, 30 October, at 19:30 CET (18:30 UK time), followed by FP2 at 23:00 CET (22:00 UK time). Teams will use the two sessions to gather data and assess their setups on a circuit where the thin air can significantly affect car performance.

Saturday's action begins with FP3 at 18:30 CET (17:30 UK time), providing one final opportunity to make adjustments before qualifying starts at 22:00 CET (21:00 UK time).

George Russell and Kimi Antonelli during 2025 Mexican Grand Prix

The race itself is scheduled for Sunday, 1 November, at 21:00 CET (20:00 UK time), bringing the weekend to its conclusion after 71 laps around the 4.304-kilometre circuit.

For Antonelli, the stakes extend far beyond another race victory. The Mercedes driver has the chance to turn an outstanding campaign into a championship-winning season, with Mexico City potentially becoming the scene of his greatest achievement yet.
