articles.title: 'I don't think we can reveal on live TV': Shadab Khan on chat with Haris Rauf
articles.summary: Shadab Khan led a remarkable comeback for Pakistan against England by scoring an unbeaten 113 runs. Together with Haris Rauf, they built a record-breaking pa...
articles.body:
Pakistan all-rounder Shadab Khan had plenty to say about his conversation with Haris Rauf during their match-winning partnership against England. After guiding Pakistan to a thrilling one-wicket win in Lahore on Sunday, Shadab revealed that the two were talking more about things other than cricket. "He was explaining things to me more than I was explaining things to him. He was saying things along the way that I don't think we can reveal on live TV. I think we had a lot of fun moments and really enjoyed ourselves. We were talking more about other things than cricket," Shadab said after being named Player of the Match. Their conversation seemed to work wonders as Pakistan pulled off a remarkable comeback. Chasing 242, the hosts were struggling at 154-9 before Shadab and Rauf joined hands to take the team home.

Shadab remained unbeaten on 113, while Rauf scored seven not out off 19 balls. The pair added 89 runs for the last wicket, the highest partnership for the final wicket in a successful ODI run chase. Pakistan needed a strong finish after England's bowlers had put them on the back foot. Shadab struck 13 fours and five sixes to lead the fightback, while Rauf played a crucial supporting role. Shadab was given out lbw with Pakistan needing 21 runs to win. However, he reviewed the decision and survived after replays showed an inside edge. Reflecting on the partnership, Shadab said Rauf deserved more credit for helping Pakistan cross the finish line. "Obviously, you only enjoy an innings when the team wins. So, I'm very happy that I played that innings and we won the match. I think Haris deserves more credit than me because, obviously, tailenders at that position are always keen to hit sixes. The way I was guiding him, or he was guiding me, we managed to put together a good partnership."

Shadab reveals what kept him going at 154-9

Pakistan looked close to defeat when Shadab found himself with the last man at the crease. However, the all-rounder said he kept believing that he could finish the job. "Obviously, I think you just go with the flow. When I made my comeback in the last series, there was an innings against Australia where I kept going until the end, but I couldn't win the match. So the idea was to keep believing. The conditions were a little different today, with dew coming in. I also felt their bowling was under a bit of pressure, given how things had gone in the previous match. I thought that if we could put them under pressure, they might end up bowling in areas that suited my game."

Afridi's four wickets put England under pressure

Earlier, England were bowled out for 241 in 46.4 overs after Ben Duckett scored a composed 105. Shaheen Shah Afridi led Pakistan's bowling attack with four wickets for 46 runs. Afridi struck in the first over to dismiss Tom Banton and removed Joe Root in the third. Haris Rauf then sent Jordan Cox back as England slipped to 52-4. Duckett and Sam Curran rebuilt the innings with a 93-run partnership for the fifth wicket. Curran scored 42 before becoming Afridi's third victim. Jamie Overton helped England cross 200, while Gus Atkinson remained unbeaten on 36. Pakistan's chase also got off to a poor start as Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam fell for 10 each. Saad Baig scored a quick 32 off 22 balls, while Salman Ali Agha made 26, but Pakistan continued to lose wickets. Shadab arrived at the crease in the 24th over with Pakistan at 103-6. His unbeaten century eventually turned the match around and secured a place for the hosts in the tri-series final. The defeat was England's third consecutive loss in the tri-series. They had earlier suffered a heavy blow when Sri Lanka chased down 430 with one ball remaining, completing the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola handpicks Liverpool's next Mohamed Salah
articles.summary: Mohamed Salah still hasn't been properly replaced at Liverpool. The attacker mutually agreed to terminate his contract at the end of last season and, even th...
articles.body:
Mohamed Salah still hasn't been properly replaced at Liverpool.

The attacker mutually agreed to terminate his contract at the end of last season and, even though the Reds didn't get any sort of transfer fee for him, they did manage to save around £20 million on his years worth of wages.

If he'd have stayed, the Egyptian King would only have a year left on his deal anyway and, with the way that Andoni Iraola's system works , it's unclear how things would have turned out for him.

Indeed, others such as Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz were added to Liverpool's ranks but, since they're both natural left-wingers rather than right-wingers, there's still a gap in the Reds' first-team squad that needs to be plugged.

So, the fact that Iraola now seems to have chosen his very own version of Salah should be music to the ears of Liverpool fans.

David Otorbi could become Liverpool's next Mohamed Salah

Recently, news has broken which shared that Liverpool were willing to activate the €30 million release clause that was baked within David Otorbi's Valencia contract.

The Spaniard has recently broken onto the La Liga scene and, although he has managed to contribute to many goals yet, his performances have caught the eye of Liverpool.

Not only is he one of Valencia's fastest players but, he's also one of their best despite only being 19 years old.

Several other clubs from around the world have been linked with an interest in him but, since he's a natural right-winger and is currently looking for his big break, it feels like he could become the Reds' next Salah.

Indeed, he is right-footed so he won't be an exact carbon copy but, playstyle wise, Otorbi looks like the perfect successor.

Liverpool must make their move for David Otorbi soon if they want to sign him

Liverpool's interest in Otorbi has only just emerged.

The Spaniard wasn't on the radar of any other clubs with Liverpool being one of the first teams linked with an actual interest in him.

But, now that Valencia look likely to extend his deal and bump his release clause up to €60 million, the Reds are going to have to act fast if they want to sign him.

Knowing the La Liga outfit, they'll try and hold out for the €60 million clause but, if they have another terrible season, as they did last term, they may not have that option to rely upon by the end of the term.

At the moment, Liverpool's attack seems to be in a fairly solid place with some such as Cody Gakpo , Alexander Isak and even Bradley Barcola now getting back to their best .

But, if Iraola and Julian Ward want to best prepare their attack for the future, Otorbi could be the best way for them to do that.

articles.title: Antonelli superb and Leclerc close to perfect - driver ratings
articles.summary: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the United States Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli sealed his ninth victory of the season with victory at the United States Grand Prix in Austin.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was second and Red Bull's Max Verstappen third.

Mercedes' Antonelli, 20, can become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history if he finishes ninth or higher at the Mexico City Grand Prix next weekend.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Texas.

A superb weekend under the added pressure of having his first opportunity to seal the championship. Produced an outstanding lap for pole and then controlled the race beautifully, making the one-stop work while many around him needed two.

Very close to a perfect weekend himself. Fastest in both Friday practice sessions, qualified fourth and then raced brilliantly in his Ferrari to second, including late passes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen.

Quick all weekend and put the Red Bull on the front row, but the poor start immediately made his race more difficult. Recovered well despite problems with the car and still came away with a sixth consecutive podium.

Another strong weekend but behind team-mate Leclerc for the majority of it. Fastest in final practice, only narrowly behind Leclerc in qualifying and fought his way back to fourth after Ferrari committed to the two-stop strategy.

Recovered well from eighth on the grid but qualifying should have been better as his quickest Q3 lap was deleted for track limits. McLaren's decision to leave him out on ageing tyres cost him late on, so fifth was not entirely of his own making.

An excellent turnaround after struggling badly with the Red Bull during practice. Qualified a superb third, ran strongly in the race and eventually finished sixth despite throttle mapping problems and moving aside for team-mate Verstappen.

A fairly subdued weekend by the McLaren man's standards. Seventh in qualifying and seventh in the race, although the first-lap battle with George Russell went against him and the stewards decided the Mercedes driver was at fault.

A disappointing weekend given what the other Mercedes achieved. Admitted both of his Q3 laps were poor and then picked up a five-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in his battle with Piastri, eventually finishing eighth.

Another quietly excellent weekend from Lawson. Racing Bulls sacrificed a proper Q3 attempt to preserve tyres for Sunday and he converted ninth on the grid into ninth at the finish to score again.

Probably extracted just about everything available from the Alpine. Missed Q3 but fought his way back into the points after an early dice with Haas' Oliver Bearman.

Another solid if unspectacular weekend for the Audi driver. Just missed Q3 and spent Sunday on the fringes of the points before eventually finishing 11th.

Reaching Q3 was an excellent effort after admitting team-mate Lawson had been quicker than him for much of the weekend. A power-unit penalty dropped him from ninth to 14th on the grid and he recovered a couple of positions to 12th.

A much better weekend than 13th suggests. Produced what he described as one of his best qualifying laps before helping team-mate Hulkenberg with a tow, then recovered from 21st on the grid after an enormous power-unit penalty.

Out in Q1 and again lacked the pace team-mate Bearman had shown earlier in the weekend. Gained places at the start and Haas eventually prioritised his undamaged car, but 14th was all he could manage.

Started from the pit lane after Aston Martin made changes to the car and fitted additional power unit components, so 15th represented a reasonable recovery. Beat team-mate Fernando Alonso to the flag after a weekend where neither car looked particularly competitive.

Getting the Aston Martin into Q2 was encouraging and penalties initially promoted him to 12th on the grid. But he went backwards on Sunday and contact with Williams' Alex Albon didn't help as he eventually finished behind Stroll after a slow pit stop.

Williams knew this circuit would expose the weaknesses of their car and that proved to be the case. Qualified behind team-mate Carlos Sainz but at least he recovered to lead the team home after an eventful opening part of the race.

A mistake late in his final qualifying lap contributed to a Q1 exit on a weekend when Williams were already struggling badly. Finished behind Albon and never looked capable of rescuing points from a difficult weekend.

Beat team-mate Valtteri Bottas in qualifying despite suffering an energy-recovery issue on his final lap. But Cadillac simply didn't have competitive pace at their home race, and P19 was a fairly anonymous result.

Qualified last before eventually retiring late enough to trigger the final virtual safety car. There wasn't much evidence across the weekend that Cadillac had the performance to achieve anything significant.

Qualified 14th but a 10-place power-unit penalty left the Alpine driver effectively starting from the back. His retirement meant there was little opportunity to turn the weekend around.

There had been real promise after he led Haas throughout Friday and initially looked quick enough for 13th in qualifying before losing his lap to track limits. Sunday unravelled with contact, a penalty and damage before he eventually retired.
authors: Harry Benjamin - BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator in Austin

articles.title: Texans’ Jaylin Noel injury update puts further damper on Giants loss
articles.summary: The Houston Texans failed to extend their winning streak in Week 7, suffering a 27-21 loss against the New York Giants. Additionally, Jaylin Noel’s injury ma...
articles.body:
The Houston Texans failed to extend their winning streak in Week 7, suffering a 27-21 loss against the New York Giants. Additionally, Jaylin Noel's injury made the loss even more frustrating for Houston, and the latest update on the wide receiver's condition has raised further concerns.

After the game, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed that Noel had suffered a turf toe injury and was still undergoing evaluation.

"DeMeco Ryans said Jaylin Noel has a turf toe injury, which is why he didn't return. He's wearing a boot," Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Texans reported.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Noel sustained the injury during a kickoff return in the fourth quarter against New York, forcing him to exit the game early. He finished with two receptions on two targets for minus-three receiving yards. The Texans star also contributed on special teams, returning a kickoff for 21 yards and recording an 11-yard punt return before his afternoon came to an end.

The Houston team struggled to get their receiving corps going throughout the game. Nico Collins managed just two receptions for six yards, while Noel's early departure further limited Houston's options in the passing game. Though the Texans managed to force overtime, their offensive struggles ultimately proved costly as they failed to secure the victory.

The injury was particularly disappointing because Noel had shown encouraging signs in the previous game. He recorded 107 receiving yards against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 6.

Houston's upcoming bye week could provide Noel with valuable recovery time. The Texans will have an additional week to evaluate the injury and determine whether the receiver can return without aggravating the problem.

However, turf toe injuries can vary in severity. Hence, his recovery timeline will depend on the results of further evaluation.

The loss dropped Houston to 2-5, while the Giants improved to 4-2-1 heading into their bye week .

articles.title: La razón que nadie cuenta por la que no debes esperar a fin de año si quieres un coche con 'etiqueta 0'
articles.standfirst: Las ayudas del Plan Auto+ están gastando sus fondos para 2026. El problema es que no hay financiación aprobada para el próximo año y viene otra complicación añadida
articles.summary: Las ayudas del Plan Auto+ están gastando sus fondos para 2026. El problema es que no hay financiación aprobada para el próximo año y viene otra complicación añadida
articles.body: Desde el 1 de enero de 2026, quienes compran un coche con 'etiqueta 0' de la DGT pueden acogerse al Plan Auto+, el programa de ayudas del Gobierno para animar las ventas de coches eléctricos e híbridos enchufables. La iniciativa se puso en marcha con un presupuesto de 400 millones de euros para este año y permite recibir hasta 4.500 euros de por la compra de un turismo, a los que se suma un descuento mínimo de 1.000 euros que debe aplicar el concesionario. En el mejor de los casos, la rebaja alcanzar los 5.500 euros. Eso sí, alcanzar este tope requiere unas condiciones: para los turismos existe un límite de precio de 45.000 euros sin contar con impuestos, y la cuantía final depende de factores como el grado de electrificación (no es lo mismo 100% eléctrico, que híbrido enchufable o de autonomía extendida), que el montaje final del coche se haga en Europa (esto, suma un 15%) o que las baterías hayan sido ensambladas en Europa y cumplan unos criterios de sostenibilidad. Además, la ayuda se aplica de forma retroactiva a las compras realizadas desde el 1 de enero, aunque el plazo para presentar las solicitudes de los particulares no se abrió hasta el pasado 4 de agosto. Este programa reserva 350 millones de euros para particulares y 50 millones, para empresas y profesionales autónomos. Los autónomos y las microempresas pueden recibir hasta 6.000 euros por un turismo y hasta 7.500 euros por una furgoneta ligera, mientras que para las empresas de mayor tamaño los máximos son de 4.500 y 5.000 euros, respectivamente. Ahora bien, este programa tiene una fecha de caducidad: el 31 de diciembre a las 14h. Y eso si no termina antes, porque también puede suceder de que se agoten los recursos. Y aquí empieza el problema que debería tener en cuenta quien esté pensando en cambiar de coche en los próximos meses. Antes que nada, no nos pongamos alarmistas; según los últimos datos disponibles del Ministerio de Industria (a 16 de octubre), se han presentado ya solicitudes por valor de 283,74 millones de euros. Es decir, vamos aproximadamente por el 71% de los 400 millones habilitados para 2026. A ese ritmo, no parece muy fácil que llegue a agotarse el presupuesto. Pero conviene aclarar que una cosa es haber solicitado ese dinero, y otra muy distinta haberlo recibido, ya que para esto último los plazos se están demorando entre dos y cuatro meses (con el antiguo Plan Moves III había que esperar entre uno y dos años). Pero el motivo más importante para no dejar la decisión de compra para el último momento no está solo en el dinero que queda. La incertidumbre afecta también a lo que ocurrirá cuando termine la convocatoria actual. De momento no existe una partida prevista que garantice la continuidad de las subvenciones el próximo año. Es cierto que el Plan España Auto 2030, que es la hoja de ruta diseñada por el Gobierno y el sector para impulsar la electrificación y reforzar la automovilística, contempla mantener las ayudas. Sin embargo los fondos para cada ejercicio deben ser sacados adelante aunque sea mediante decreto-ley. El factor que viene a complicar todo un poquito más son las elecciones generales del próximo 29 de noviembre. Y más en concreto, el hecho de que hasta que se forme un nuevo Gobierno y se definan sus prioridades presupuestarias podrían pasar varios meses. Esta es la razón por la que, entre los fabricantes de coches, cunde ya cierto temor ante la posibilidad de que se retrase la puesta en marcha del plan de 2027. Y si no hay compromiso de ayudas, el cliente de a pie preferirá esperar. Sabiendo esto, y el hecho de que los concesionarios suelen afinar sus ofertas a final de año, una parte de los compradores puede adelantar su decisión de compra para aprovechar las subvenciones actuales. Si las ayudas desaparecen temporalmente, esa combinación amenaza con provocar un bache en las ventas de coches eléctricos e híbridos enchufables durante los primeros meses del año, aunque sea muy posible que después se apliquen con carácter retroactivo a todo coche comprado desde el 1 de enero. No sería la primera vez que unas elecciones generan incertidumbres a la hora de comprar coches. El anterior Plan MOVES III dejó expedientes pendientes y estuvo condicionado por la disponibilidad de fondos en las comunidades autónomas. Por ello, el Auto+ nació, entre otras cosas, para simplificar la gestión mediante un sistema centralizado. Pero esa mejora administrativa no resuelve por sí sola la incertidumbre sobre la financiación futura. Lo que no existe hoy es una garantía de que vaya a hacerse ni una fecha confirmada para una eventual convocatoria de 2027. Por eso, quien tenga decidido comprar un coche con 'etiqueta 0' tal vez haga bien en no esperar a final de año, porque pasar esta fecha puede suponer bastantes meses de espera hasta que salga el nuevo plan y se puedan cobrar unas ayudas que, a día de hoy, no están oficialmente garantizadas.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli wins US Grand Prix, closes in on F1 championship
articles.summary: Mercedes’s 20-year-old driver can win the championship in Mexico next week if his teammate Russell doesn’t win the race.
articles.body:
Italian wunderkind Kimi Antonelli took another step toward his first Formula One championship by claiming his ninth race of the year at the United States Grand Prix in Austin, Texas.

Antonelli, 20, capitalised on his pole position and sailed to a time of 1:35:16.650 at the Circuit of the Americas on Sunday, beating Charles Leclerc of Monaco by a comfortable 13.078 seconds.

With five races to go, Antonelli does not have the championship wrapped up quite yet, but his lead over Mercedes teammate George Russell of Great Britain expanded to 123 points.

Russell must win the next race in Mexico City to remain in contention for the championship; otherwise, it will go to Antonelli, who has come to dominate the sport in his second F1 campaign.

“I’m aware [securing the championship] is close, but the mindset doesn’t change,” Antonelli said post-race. “I want to finish the season on a high, to go into 2027 with high hopes.”

The strategy for Antonelli and Mercedes paid off. While others chose to pit twice during the 56-lap race, Antonelli held on until Lap 25 to pit and did not visit the pit lane again.

“It was a perfect way to end the weekend; it was an incredible team effort, especially from strategy to believe in me and go for one stop,” Antonelli said.

Antonelli won five Grands Prix in a row early this season, one of which was the Miami Grand Prix. He is now 2-for-2 in the United States this season, with the Las Vegas Grand Prix still to come in November.

Max Verstappen, the four-time F1 champion for Red Bull Racing, rounded out the podium 17.485 seconds behind Antonelli. After rattling off every championship from 2021 to 2024, Verstappen has been mathematically eliminated from this year’s chase and will go two years without a world title.

“Our overall pace was not good enough, and the tyres we had available were not the right ones,” Verstappen said. “We still managed to get on the podium, maybe a bit lucky with the [Virtual Safety Car] at the end.”

A Virtual Safety Car was deployed after Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac stopped on the track on Lap 52. It lasted until the penultimate lap, by which time nobody would be catching up to Antonelli.

Mercedes grew its lead in the constructors’ standings to 133 points over Ferrari — 607 points to Ferrari’s 474.

“On Kimi’s side, the main headline is that for me [that’s] the best race that he’s delivered so far,” Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff said.

“Getting off the start with the inferior tyre and then controlling it [the race] at all times. The race of a champion who isn’t the champion yet, but exceptional.

“I think he’s outperformed the car. His driving style just glues with the car.”

Wolff, reminded that Antonelli has had some special wins already this season, including at his home Italian Grand Prix from the back of the grid as well as Monaco and Spa , accepted that sometimes he struggled to remember past races.

“Both of them were pretty good,” he said in reference to Monza. “But the headline, this is the best, we can keep.”

Antonelli was happy to agree with the boss.

“I think it was one of the best, because of how we built up during the weekend,” he told reporters.

“And, you know, it was a great team effort as well today, especially with the strategy, believing in the one-stop. And, yeah, it was a really great team effort, and they all deserve this result today.

“Monza, we clearly had the fastest car. We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back,” he added.

“But it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake, and we were so quick. But definitely, Monza was a super special one, and one that I will remember forever. But, you know, this one probably, in terms of execution, was better … the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good.”

articles.title: Saudi Arabia confirms January start for Asian Cup 2027 despite attacks
articles.summary: Asian Cup 2027 to kick off on January 7 with Saudi Arabia facing Palestine in Riyadh as the AFC announces the schedule.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia will host the 2027 Asian Cup in January and February despite recent doubts surrounding the tournament’s schedule due to ongoing attacks on the country and wider regional unrest.

The continental championship will get under way on January 7 in Riyadh, where the hosts will take on Palestine in a Group A fixture, according to the tournament schedule announced by the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) on Monday.

Riyadh’s 72,000-seat King Fahd Sports City Stadium will also host the inaugural match and serve as the venue for the final on February 5.

Eight venues – five in Riyadh, two in Jeddah and one in Al-Khobar – will host the 51 matches across the 29-day tournament.

Despite the confirmation from the organisers, the tournament’s fate remains under scrutiny as several of the 24 participating federations have raised concerns about security in the region.

Earlier on Monday, organisers of the Dakar Rally said the race would be moved out of Saudi Arabia for the 2027 edition due to the “recent developments in the region”.

Last week, a top Japanese football official said the ongoing security situation in Saudi Arabia would make it difficult for the country to host the Asian Cup as scheduled.

“Based on what I’ve learned from the news, the situation is still unsafe, so at this point, I don’t think it would be easy to hold the [Asian] Cup there,” Japan Football Association President Tsuneyasu Miyamoto said.

“I just had a meeting with the Saudi side, and they said that their top priority is the safety of the players, the fans and everyone who would be attending the tournament.”

Several major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have been cancelled or postponed amid escalating attacks by Yemen’s Houthis.

The Saudi-led coalition intercepted a barrage of projectiles from Yemen that targeted cities across the kingdom on Sunday.

The Saudi Civil Defence said shrapnel from two intercepted ballistic missiles, suspected to have been fired by Yemen’s Houthis, fell in Jeddah, Taif, Rabigh and Wadi Al-Mughammas in Mecca province.

The kingdom has faced waves of Houthi missile and drone attacks in recent weeks that have targeted civilian and military infrastructure.

Riyadh announced late on Saturday that international flights from King Khalid International Airport would resume from Terminal 2 on Sunday while Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights.

This follows the suspension of flights from the Riyadh airport after waves of Houthi strikes, including one on 10 October that killed 13 people and wounded hundreds.

AFC chief Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa said this month that a postponement of the continental championships until 2028 was possible if necessary, but the local organising committee said it was sticking to the original schedule.

Defending champions Qatar will begin their title defence against Thailand on January 11 while Japan will open ⁠⁠their campaign against Indonesia the same day.

South Korea will face Yemen, ⁠⁠Australia will take on Singapore ⁠⁠and Iran will meet China in their opening matches.

The tournament’s group stage concludes on January 20 with the knockout rounds ‌‌beginning on January 22.

Saudi Arabia will host the Asian Cup for the first time, ‌‌seven ‌‌years before it stages the 2034 World Cup.

images.caption: Saudi Arabia is scheduled to face Palestine in the opening match of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup in Riyadh on January 7 [File: Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana/Reuters]

articles.title: BS Meter on Dylan Larkin, Travis Konecny and the Latest NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: We've had our first blockbuster NHL trade since the puck dropped on the 2026-27 regular season on Sept. 29. On Friday, the Winnipeg Jets shipped superstar goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils in a multi-player deal.
articles.body:
We've had our first blockbuster NHL trade since the puck dropped on the 2026-27 regular season on Sept. 29. On Friday, the Winnipeg Jets shipped superstar goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils in a multi-player deal .

In today's salary-cap era, trades of that magnitude rarely occur this early in the season. With the rising salary cap giving clubs more cap space to work with, some of them are able to make big deals much earlier.

It could lead to more notable players getting moved during the autumn months instead of waiting until the March trade deadline, when teams have accrued sufficient salary-cap room to make those moves. Some teams could attempt to address roster issues now before they become bigger problems.

The rumor mill keeps churning, but which of the latest notable rumors should we believe? Follow along as we use our trusty BS Meter to assess which reports look credible—and which seem unlikely.

Will the Toronto Maple Leafs Pursue a Defenseman?

The revamped Toronto Maple Leafs are off to a good start after missing the playoffs last season. However, the recent loss of oft-injured shutdown defenseman Chris Tanev has raised concerns about how the Maple Leafs can replace him.

On Oct. 14, Jonas Siegel of The Athletic speculated that Tanev's latest injury could send general manager John Chayka into the trade market. Given the 36-year-old blueliner's history, Siegel believed there are no guarantees that he won't get hurt again.

Three days later, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the Maple Leafs had informed teams they're not interested in "band-aid solutions." He said they're willing to part with a "premium asset" for a difference-maker on their blue line.

Friedman also said the Maple Leafs were willing to move an older player for a younger one. However, he didn't indicate which Leafs would be available or which younger defenseman they could be watching.

The Maple Leafs are 5-2-1 since Tanev was sidelined on Oct. 10 , meaning Chayka can afford to be patient. However, his penchant for bold moves suggests he'll monitor the trade market for affordable defensemen to bolster his blue line.

Could the Columbus Blue Jackets Trade Dmitri Voronkov?

Before the regular season began, the Columbus Blue Jackets swung a six-player trade with the Toronto Maple Leafs. The centerpiece was winger Kirill Marchenko, whom the Blue Jackets traded to the Maple Leafs for winger Matthew Knies.

Following that blockbuster deal, the Blue Jackets stumbled to a 4-5-0 record. By Oct. 25, they were sitting at the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings.

They risk becoming an also-ran unless they shake things up. That could force general manager Don Waddell to consider moving another player.

On Oct. 22, TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported that some teams were calling the Blue Jackets about winger Dmitri Voronkov. LeBrun couldn't say whether the 6'5", 230-pounder would be traded for sure, but claimed the Jackets were listening to offers.

Voronkov is slated to become a restricted free agent with arbitration rights next July, when he'll also be a year away from unrestricted free-agent eligibility. If the big 26-year-old winger won't sign a long-term extension, Waddell could peddle him before the March 1 trade deadline.

Could the Pittsburgh Penguins Trade a Veteran Player?

Expectations were high for the Pittsburgh Penguins after the retooling club surprised experts last season by clinching a playoff berth. However, hopes of improvement this season are fading following a 5-6-1 record through their first 12 games , including just two wins in their last nine contests (2-6-1).

On Oct. 17, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that the Penguins were willing to trade a veteran forward for draft picks and prospects. He said they wanted to create room on the roster to give more playing time to their younger players.

Six days later, TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported that Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas was open to offers for some of his veteran players. He believes Dubas is listening on defensemen Erik Karlsson and Kris Letang, and forwards Rickard Rakell and Bryan Rust.

Karlsson ($10 million) is slated to become an unrestricted free agent on July 1. Letang ($6.1 million average annual value), Rust ($5.125 million), and Rakell ($5 million) are signed through 2027-28 .

Karlsson has a full no-movement clause. Letang has a no-movement clause with a 10-team approved trade list, Rakell has a modified no-trade clause, and Rust lacks no-trade protection.

Dubas has been transitioning his roster toward younger players over the past two seasons. With the Penguins struggling, it's not surprising he's open to trade proposals for aging players not named Sidney Crosby or Evgeni Malkin.

Will the Philadelphia Flyers Trade Travis Konecny?

The Philadelphia Flyers' season-opening nine-game winless skid (0-6-3) raised concern among the club's followers. During a 4-1 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes on Oct. 11, their fans called for head coach Rick Tocchet to be fired and booed the team off the ice at the end of the game.

That skid also sparked speculation about whether Flyers general manager Daniel Briere would make a trade or two before the season got out of reach. Longtime winger Travis Konecny (currently on injured reserve ) was among the players mentioned as potential trade chips.

On Oct. 13, Daily Faceoff's Anthony Di Marco included the 29-year-old Konecny among his list of trade candidates. He cited team sources claiming there was some frustration within the organization about his performance, suggesting he might be asked to waive his no-movement clause if the club didn't improve.

After the Flyers finally picked up their first two wins, Di Marco subsequently reported that winger Owen Tippett was drawing more interest from other clubs than Konecny, likely because of the latter's NMC. However, he felt Konecny was the better trade candidate because of his all-around play.

Flyers beat writer Kevin Kurz of The Athletic and Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman were skeptical . Kurz cited Konecny's contract and commitment to the team, calling it " incredibly unlikely " that the Flyers would trade the player who's led them in scoring for five of the last six seasons.

Are the Montreal Canadiens in the Market for a Center ... Including Dylan Larkin?

After reaching the Eastern Conference Final last season, the Montreal Canadiens were expected to take another step toward Stanley Cup contention this season. However, their inconsistent start (6-3-2) has raised concerns among Montreal fans and pundits.

That worry reached new heights when team captain Nick Suzuki injured his hand during an Oct. 20 game against the San Jose Sharks. The 27-year-old Selke Trophy winner is sidelined for two to four weeks, prompting Adam Proteau of The Hockey News to wonder if the Canadiens would shop for a center.

On Oct. 22, TSN's Pierre LeBrun said he believed there's a chance Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin might include the Canadiens on his trade list. They're not on his current list, which he recently expanded to 10 teams.

LeBrun reported that the Red Wings are actively scouting the Canadiens, among other teams, saying they were conducting due diligence in case Larkin adds them to his list. He also claimed the Habs' interest in the Red Wings' center predates Suzuki's injury.

BS Meter: Not BS, but not necessarily for Larkin

Larkin hasn't included any Canadian teams on his trade list, so a move to Montreal would require him to expand it.

The Canadiens will remain patient since Suzuki isn't out for the long term, but his absence could put more urgency on their efforts to land a reliable top-six center.

articles.title: 6 Predictions on the Road to WWE Survivor Series WarGames 2026
articles.summary: The road to WWE Survivor Series: WarGames 2026 is shaping up to be an interesting one in light of recent events on Raw and SmackDown.
articles.body:
The road to WWE Survivor Series: WarGames 2026 is shaping up to be an interesting one in light of recent events on Raw and SmackDown.

Crown Jewel is the next major event on Nov. 7, and what transpires there is sure to set the stage for Survivor Series at the end of the month. Three matches are currently confirmed for Crown Jewel and more are expected to be added over the next two weeks.

In the meantime, WWE is advertising several major matches for upcoming episodes of the red and blue brands including CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens and Bayley vs. Lyra Valkyria in a No Disqualification match. The results of those bouts should have a direct impact on the build for Survivor Series as well.

With this being the time of year that WWE tends to phone in creatively, it's imperative that they heat up their programming in a major way and give viewers more of an incentive to tune in. Whether that means continuing certain feuds or starting new ones, the next month-plus of WWE TV must be meaningful to ensure the Thanksgiving week classic feels as special as it should be.

These are six predictions for the remainder of the road to Survivor Series: WarGames.

CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens Ends Without a Winner

On the Oct. 23 edition of SmackDown, it was announced that CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens will take place on the final episode before Crown Jewel.

Although it would have been a logical addition to the event itself, it will also make for a marquee matchup in the main event of SmackDown, much like their original encounter back in August.

Punk and Owens have been at odds since soon after SummerSlam but have yet to settle their score decisively. Their upcoming clash set for SmackDown could be the blow-off, but more than likely, it will simply serve as the next chapter in their story.

Recently, Sami Zayn has been busy rekindling his rivalries with Roman Reigns and Trick Williams. As such, he hasn't been as involved in Punk and Owens' affairs as he was prior to Money in the Bank.

A Triple Threat between the three of them for the Undisputed WWE Championship should be the endgame at Survivor Series, and that can only happen if Punk and Owens' rematch ends without a proper finish.

WWE just did something similar with the Raw women's division, so it would hardly feel fresh, but neither Punk nor Owens should be losing their match.

Both should be in line for a title opportunity at Survivor Series, so perhaps Zayn can lay them both out to send a message to Reigns ahead of Crown Jewel and create the need for a Triple Threat that way.

Bayley Sets Sights on Women's World Championship

Bayley and Lyra Valkyria's rivalry has lasted long enough, but thankfully it is expected to culminate when they collide in a No Disqualification match on Monday's Raw.

With Valkyria having won their first two encounters, Bayley looks like the logical pick to win the finale.

In theory, that should set up The Role Model for an opportunity at the Women's World Championship.

Of course, the odds of her actually taking the title from Liv Morgan at this stage are slim to none, but if nothing else, she'd be a credible challenger to keep the titleholder busy until Morgan's next major storyline, which should ideally be with Roxanne Perez.

The Judgment Day should be featured in the 2026 women's WarGames match, and Bayley should find herself among their opponents for the bout. A big win for the Grand Slam champion inside the double cage can put her in immediate championship contention.

Bayley's pursuit of the title will begin after she conquers Valkyria and shifts her focus back to holding gold again.

Oba Femi Resumes Rivalry with The Vision

Oba Femi disposed of Bronson Reed with relative ease at Money in the Bank. On the subsequent Raw, he seemed to deny the assistance of Paul Heyman, who has been fixated on Femi since the two-time NXT champion retired his previous client, Brock Lesnar, at SummerSlam.

Heyman hasn't been officially aligned with The Vision in some time, but he could still send them to do his dirty work in the next week or two. Femi was absent from the Oct. 19 edition of Raw, so there's been no indication on what else could be next for him.

If The Ruler isn't going after the World Heavyweight Championship until closer to WrestleMania 43, the simplest solution would be to have him resume his rivalry with The Vision on the road to Survivor Series.

Femi may have beaten Reed clean, but he and Bron Breakker have unfinished business from Sunday Night's Main Event in early September. Regardless of who from The Vision he faces again, there aren't many other options for him to work with for the rest of 2026.

The Ruler stealing the tag titles from them could be an intriguing direction for him, potentially alongside Je'Von Evans, but another team should be back soon to do that instead.

Way-Too-Early WrestleMania 43 Predictions 🔮

The Street Profits Return to Target Tag Titles

It's easy to forget The Street Profits have been away from WWE TV for almost four months. They haven't been seen since losing the World Tag Team Championship back to The Vision on the July 6 edition of Raw.

Although no reason has been reported for their extended absence, Ford and Dawkins should be brought back sooner rather than later.

Once they do resurface on Raw, they should pick up where they left off by targeting the tag titles.

It's not as if the red brand has much of a division to speak of, anyway. In fact, Bron Breakker and Austin Theory haven't defended the belts a single time on television since winning them.

Oba Femi is by no means in dire need of backup, but the Profits joining forces with him and Je'Von Evans to rid Raw of The Vision would be a fine use of all involved.

Tiffany Stratton Announces Money in the Bank Cash-In

After enduring a scary fall at Money in the Bank but still managing to win the women's Money in the Bank ladder match, Tiffany Stratton resurfaced on SmackDown this past Friday to save Chelsea Green and Iyo Sky from The Judgment Day.

Stratton even teased cashing in her newly won briefcase on women's world champion Liv Morgan (much like she attempted to two years ago during her last stint as Ms. Money in the Bank). However, it couldn't be more obvious that she will eventually be cashing in on her new bestie Green.

The question is more how and when she intends to do it. Having her announce it ahead of time would be more effective than a surprise cash-in where it might be more ambiguous as to whether she was turning heel or not.

Stratton giving Green the chance to prepare for their title match would make Stratton's loss hit that much harder and serve as the perfect catalyst for her heel turn. Green still has a title defense scheduled against Nikki Bella for the Oct. 30 edition of SmackDown, so Stratton vs. Green shouldn't be until Survivor Series at the earliest.

Penta's Money in the Bank intentions are bound to remain a mystery for many more months, but Stratton's plans for the opportunistic contract should become clear extremely soon.

WWE is establishing the field for this year's men's WarGames match more and more by the week, and the big brawl that closed out the Oct. 19 edition of Raw provided fans with what was essentially a sneak peek of what it will most likely look like.

The Bloodline's team is almost guaranteed to consist of Roman Reigns, The Usos, Jacob Fatu and Solo Sikoa while Royce Keys, OTM and Carmelo Hayes will make up The 946. If WWE sticks with the usual five-on-five format, The 946 will need one more person on their team, and LA Knight would be a better fit than anyone.

Coming off his loss to Reigns at Money in the Bank, he'll feel betrayed by Sikoa reuniting with The Bloodline, and in order to eliminate the group once and for all, he'll agree to team with The 946. He won't be deemed an actual member of The 946 but merely an ally in their war with The Bloodline.

If WWE has no plans for Knight to be a world champion anytime soon, then turning him heel would be a refreshing change for his character. This would keep him in the main event mix for at least a little while longer.

With just over a month left until Survivor Series, WWE has to keep the build to WarGames exciting, and incorporating Knight into the ongoing rivalry between The Bloodline and The 946 would accomplish just that.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Jeff Hardy Injured, Stephanie Vaquer Return Update and WWE Backstage Rumors on Eric Young
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Jeff Hardy Set to Miss Time Due to Injury

Way-Too-Early WrestleMania 43 Predictions 🔮

It sounds like Matt Hardy will be on his own for a while, as his brother, Jeff, is set to address a nagging injury.

During this week's episode of The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy , the elder Hardy revealed that Jeff has been dealing with a bulging disc in his neck, and he will take some time off to recover.

"It's gonna be interesting to see what my next character is, especially if Jeff takes a little time off to try and work on his neck a little bit. That may be happening. I guess we'll see," Matt said (h/t WrestlePurists ). "It's been a year now since he's had this bulging disc that's just been bugging him. I think he's done everything he can do in his power. I think he's maybe gonna take some time off and just see what he can do to get it fixed up, and correct it as much as possible."

The Hardys most recently teamed together on the Oct. 13 episode of TNA Impact, defeating AJ Francis & Expressions. The veterans lost to syX (Joseph Sawyer & Samuel Shaw) in a Falls Count Anywhere match at the Bound For Glory pay-per-view.

Jeff Hardy is known as one of the most exciting wrestlers of all time, but it's no secret that it's taken a toll on his body. Fans will be patient as they wait for him to recover before returning to the ring.

Former WWE Women's World Champion Stephanie Vaquer appears to be on her way back to the ring, and she already knows who she's targeting.

After suffering an ankle injury when she lost her title to Liv Morgan in a Triple Threat match that also included Becky Lynch at the Money in the Bank premium live event, Vaquer announced on social media that she's off crutches and cleared to return, and she sent a message to Lynch.

"Becky, you wanted to know when I'm cleared? See you Monday," Vaquer said .

After Vaquer's announcement, Raw general manager Adam Pearce announced that her showdown against Lynch will be a No. 1 contender's match for Morgan's title.

Vaquer admitted after her Money in the Bank match against Morgan was legitimate and not part of a storyline after she was seen visibly limping and getting help from referee Jessika Carr before making her way backstage.

Now that she's back to 100 percent, Vaquer will look to settle things with Lynch before turning her attention back to Morgan and the Women's World Championship.

After reports surfaced earlier this year that Eric Young departed TNA and rejoined WWE, more details have emerged about his role.

During a recent Q&A (h/t WrestlePurists ), PWInsider's Mike Johnson reported that Young returned to WWE in July as a producer for NXT.

F4WOnline's Bryan Alvarez previously reported that Young was "expected to be a 'player/coach' in NXT." However, Johnson didn't mention whether the 46-year-old will also be competing in the ring in addition to his backstage duties.

After spending 12 years in TNA, Young joined WWE in 2016 and remained with the company until he was part of the roster cuts in 2020. He returned in 2022 but didn't appear on television, and he was back with TNA a year later.

Young has a veteran mind that will surely be beneficial to the young talent in NXT, so his return to the company will be welcomed by fans and wrestlers alike.

articles.title: Dani Pedrosa se deja llevar por un robotaxi de Tesla en Austin... y alucina
articles.standfirst: El tricampeón del mundo de motociclismo se subió a un Tesla Cybercab... y puso esta cara
articles.summary: El tricampeón del mundo de motociclismo se subió a un Tesla Cybercab... y puso esta cara
articles.body: Es muy difícil ver a un piloto de carreras cederle el volante a alguien en un coche, y menos aún si es dejarle el control del vehículo... al propio coche. Pero esto es exactamente lo que ha sucedido este fin de semana en la ciudad con más coches autónomos del planeta: Austin. Que, además, acoge a los cuarteles generales de Tesla. La capital del estado de Texas ha acogido este fin de semana a los mejores pilotos del mundo con motivo del Gran Premio de EE.UU. de Fórmula 1. Además, dentro del programa había una exhibición muy especial: la de las motos de MotoGP con un español como invitado. Se trataba de Dani Pedrosa, tres veces campeón del mundo de motociclismo y con 31 triunfos en la máxima categoría en su curriculum. El ahora probador de KTM salió a pista en los días previos al Gran Premio junto a pilotos en activo como Nicoló Bulega o ex como Andrea Dovizioso, pero fuera de la pista quiso experimentar una tecnología . El catalán no dudó el alquilar un Tesla Cybercab, el taxi autónomo de la marca de Elon Musk que actualmente tiene desplegados en Austin nada menos que 460 coches. Los robotaxis de Tesla ya han recorrido más de 3,2 millones de kilómetros y desde el 3 de septiembre prestan un servicio público en Austin al que cualquier puede acceder desde la app de Tesla. Como hizo Pedrosa durante el fin de semana. Aunque el vídeo que ha publicado en sus redes sociales es corto (apenas se le ve accediendo al interior del vehículo), la expresión de su cara cuando el coche ya está en movimiento lo dice todo... Los robotaxis son uno de los negocios de futuro en los que Musk tiene puestas mayores esperanzas. De hecho, el año 2027 debería ser el de su explosión, especialmente en países como EE.UU. en los que la legislación es más permisiva con este tipo de tecnologías. De hecho, entre las intenciones de Elon Musk para el futuro está la de comercializar el Tesla Cybercab (además, a un precio bastante ventajoso teniendo en cuenta la enorme carga tecnológica que incorpora) de forma que también pueda convertirse en vehículo privado. Aunque ese es un escenario más lejano y complejo...

articles.title: Euskadi jugará el próximo Mundial de pelota en casa
articles.standfirst: Bilbao es la sede elegida por la Federación Internacional de Pelota para la próxima edición de 2030
articles.summary: Bilbao es la sede elegida por la Federación Internacional de Pelota para la próxima edición de 2030
articles.body: Bilbao será la sede del próximo Mundial de Pelota. Euskadi jugará en casa su segundo campeonato del mundo tras su estreno en Buenos Aires en el que acabó como tercera del medallero general con 12 medallas (siete oros, cuatro platas y un bronce). España quedó primera con 18 (7 oros, 9 platas y 2 bronces). Durante la ceremonia de clausura, Xavier Cazaubon, presidente de la Federación Internacional de Pelota Vasca (FIPV) entregó la bandera institucional de la Federación a la delegación del País Vasco como símbolo de la responsabilidad de organizar el próximo Mundial. Leixuri Arrizabala, diputada de Euskera, Cultura y Deporte de la Diputación Foral de Vizcaya, Gorka Iturriaga, director de Actividad Física y Deporte del Gobierno Vasco, José María Mitxelena, presidente de la Federación Vasca de Pelota Vasca y Carlos Sergio Achotegui, director general de Deporte de la Diputación Foral de Vizcaya recibieron la bandera de manos de Cazaubon. "Bilbao 2030 representa mucho más que una sede: representa el encuentro de la Pelota Vasca con una tierra profundamente ligada a sus raíces, su identidad y su historia", relata la Federación Internacional de Pelota que a finales de 2024 reconoció a la Federación Vasca como miembro de pleno derecho. Según recoge el artículo 81.2 de la Ley del Deporte, la organización de cualquier competición internacional debe contar con el respaldo del Consejo Superior de Deportes: "La realización de competiciones federativas internacionales de carácter oficial en España precisará de autorización del Consejo Superior de Deportes, en lo referente a su compatibilidad con la política exterior española y con los compromisos internacionales que el Estado pueda haber asumido". Será la cuarta vez que el Mundial de Pelota se dispute en el País Vasco. La primera edición se celebró en San Sebastián en 1952. Repitió en 1970. En 1986 fue Vitoria la ciudad mundialista. La última vez que se celebró en España fue en 2018 en Barcelona.

articles.title: WWE and AEW's Mount Rushmore for Today's Era
articles.summary: One of the most popular questions asked of wrestlers and fans alike is who they have on their Mount Rushmore of professional wrestling.
articles.body:
One of the most popular questions asked of wrestlers and fans alike is who they have on their Mount Rushmore of professional wrestling.

Larger-than-life stars such as Hulk Hogan, Ric Flair, Bruno Sammartino, The Undertaker, Bret Hart, Shawn Michaels, The Rock and "Stone Cold" Steve Austin are always among the most popular answers.

They are, after all, some of the most important contributors to the industry's long and illustrious history.

But which stars deserve spots on WWE's and All Elite Wrestling's modern-era Mount Rushmores?

Let's take a look, with each star determined based on their historical significance and the quality of their work.

AEW has only been in existence since 2019, making it far easier to compile a foursome of the most important and deserving stars in company history.

Omega was one of the faces of pro wrestling globally at the start of AEW and a guy without whom it would have been far more difficult to get the project off the ground.

He had credibility among fans, regardless of where their allegiances lay, and he was arguably the best wrestler in the world at the start of his run there.

That he became a creative centerpiece, won two world titles, battled a serious health issue to come back and still delivered an instant classic against Will Ospreay at All In 2026 certainly doesn't hurt his case for inclusion.

Debuting on night one at AEW Double or Nothing in Las Vegas, Moxley wasted little time becoming the heart and soul of the company.

One of the most decorated and respected stars on the roster, Moxley has become the "ace" of AEW, the promotion's standard-bearer and tone-setter.

Like him and his style of wrestling or not, no one can downplay his importance to the company and his success since emerging from the stands in the MGM Grand Garden Arena seven years ago.

From the moment he first set foot in an AEW ring, it was clear that MJF had the potential to become one of the company's defining homegrown stars and a future world champion.

His work belonged in the 1980s NWA; his promo skills would have been right at home in the Attitude Era, and his willingness to get heat at any cost reminded some of the territory days.

MJF was a breakout star from day one, and he was positioned as such, working with Cody Rhodes, Chris Jericho, Hangman Page and Jon Moxley in relatively short order. Throw in one of the best rivalries in company history with CM Punk, and one of the biggest business-driving programs with Adam Cole, and you have someone synonymous with AEW and its growth and evolution.

One of AEW's pillars, Allin best embodies what it means to be one of the "sickos" Tony Khan and Co. embrace. He is left of center, a completely different wrestler from anyone else on the roster, and someone who does not hesitate to throw himself in harm's way for the sake of his performance.

He moves to the beat of a drummer who may not be on planet Earth, shows no fear in any aspect of his game, and he has won the AEW world, TNT and world tag team championships.

The longtime tag team partner of the legendary Sting up until his retirement, Allin is now helping to ensure the future of the company by partnering with Steven Borden.

While there is an argument for Swerve Strickland, Hangman Page, Chris Jericho and The Young Bucks here, Allin is so representative of AEW and its philosophies that it feels wrong not to include him.

WWE has had several major stars over the last decade or so, but a handful have left indelible marks on the company, earning their places on its modern-day Mount Rushmore.

The face that runs the place. Since 2015, Reigns has been at the forefront of the company—the face on its posters and in its marketing materials. He has been its leading star on TV, too, especially since his evolution from The Big Dog to The Tribal Chief and the introduction of The Bloodline.

Reigns was so captivating in the role that his nearly four-year reign as universal champion felt warranted—a remarkable achievement in an era of constant competition for fans' attention.

He holds the record for the most WrestleMania main events, has battled many of WWE's biggest stars during his run and is enjoying the greatest in-ring stretch of his career. Acknowledge him.

Rhodes returned to WWE in 2022 and embarked on a two-year journey to become the undisputed WWE champion, captivating fans along the way.

Their support helped persuade WWE to put him, rather than The Rock, opposite Reigns in the main event of WrestleMania 40's second night. His victory over The Tribal Chief marked the beginning of a new era in WWE.

Although some creative decisions may have hurt Rhodes' run at the top of the company, he has undeniably developed into one of WWE's leading stars.

If Rhodes and Reigns are the "Stone Cold" Steve Austin and The Rock of this generation, Rollins is the Bret Hart or Shawn Michaels: He can consistently be trusted to deliver once the bell rings.

One of the most gifted wrestlers of his era, Rollins has been presented as a star on par with his peers. He has accomplished everything: won numerous major titles, slayed The Beast Incarnate, frazzled The Tribal Chief, beaten The Best in the World and pulled off two of the greatest Money in the Bank cash-ins of all time.

Rounding out the big four of this generation of WWE Superstars is CM Punk.

Yes, he returned to the company only in 2023 after nearly a decade away. Since then, however, he has delivered one of the greatest rivalries of all time with Drew McIntyre, won both the World Heavyweight and Undisputed WWE Championships and main-evented consecutive WrestleManias. He remains as popular with fans as ever.

He is in his Shawn Michaels era: a grizzled veteran enjoying a magnificent run of in-ring performances.

Love him or hate him, Punk backs up his bravado and has repeatedly proved he is almost untouchable on the mic, in the ring and even on commentary. That is enough to earn him a spot on WWE's modern-day Mount Rushmore.

Writer's note: Becky Lynch also has a strong case based on her work in the women's division. She narrowly misses out here, with Rollins and Punk taking the final two places.

articles.title: Why the post-9/11 World Series means so much to so many 25 years later
articles.summary: Despite all the fear and emotion inspired by the September 11, 2001, attacks, the 2001 Fall Classic would end up being one of the greatest World Series ever played.
articles.body: For the first time in 46 years, a sitting US president was about to throw out the first pitch in a World Series game. Deep in the bowels of Yankee Stadium, George W. Bush was being warmed up by a man wearing a softball mitt. Outside on the diamond, a fake umpire was standing near home plate with a gun and a taser concealed beneath his uniform. Above them, the stadium was rocking, so much so that the picture frames in the offices below were hanging askew. Nothing was normal on October 30, 2001: The New York Yankees were hosting the Arizona Diamondbacks for the biggest prize in baseball in a city still in shock – just 13 miles away, the debris from the World Trade Center still burned. But despite all the fear and emotion, it would end up being one of the greatest World Series ever played. A series played amid deep shock Yankees’ senior vice president of marketing Deborah Tymon has worked behind the scenes for the club for over 40 years. She had often heard her mother talk about where she was on December 7, 1941, the day the United States base at Pearl Harbor was attacked by Japan, entering the US into the Second World War. Sixty years later, they were sitting side by side on I-87, commuting towards Yankee Stadium, when they noticed the thick black smoke on the horizon spewing from the top of the World Trade Center. Her mom said, “Oh look, the restaurant must be on fire,” Tymon told CNN Sports. After parking moments later, they realized that this was so much more serious. “At Yankee Stadium, there’s a television on the wall every five feet, in your offices and at the switchboard,” she said. “We arrived in time to see the second plane hit, and I remember thinking back to my mother telling the story of Pearl Harbor. I had this incredible image of exactly where I was standing, which TV I was looking at, when the plane hit. I think the overwhelming emotion was just fear.” Arizona Diamondbacks outfielder David Dellucci was about to get into his truck to drive to a radio station for a morning show when he checked his phone; he says there were about 30 messages. “The phone just continues to beep with message after message,” he told CNN Sports. “The first one is from the radio station; it says, ‘Don’t worry about coming in today, we, you know, we’ve got much more to cover.’” Then his family began texting, “Are you OK?” He went back inside and turned on his television. “As I’m talking and describing this, the hair on the back of my neck is standing up because it was unfathomable,” he said. Nobody thought much about baseball for a few days. The Yankees sent all the food they had in-house for a homestand to help the volunteers at Ground Zero. The organization had been personally impacted – two employees’ sons worked for Cantor Fitzgerald and perished in the North Tower. When Major League Baseball resumed six days later, Dellucci says it was hard for anyone to focus on the game. “Every airplane that flew near the field, it was almost as if the game stopped; you would look in the sky, follow the plane and then focus back on the pitch,” he said. “We never knew if we were going to get attacked again.” A series unlike any other The Diamondbacks played their first game as a new franchise in 1998, and they couldn’t have imagined that they’d make it to the World Series just three years later. From their first year to 2001, all they ever knew was a New York Yankees team that won every season, taking baseball’s ultimate prize in ’98, 1999 and 2000. Outside of the Bronx, everybody hated the Yankees – until the 2001 World Series, when the nation’s sympathies were extended to the team in pinstripes. Even Dellucci, who had dreamed of winning the World Series since he was six years old, admits he was conflicted. He visited Ground Zero with 14 of his teammates, grappling with the enormity of the tragedy. They met families of the victims and observed the “humongous bulldozers” that looked more like ants amidst the catastrophic destruction; they smelled the stench and winced at the sight of first responders removing names from a board whenever they identified a corpse or a body part. “When we got on the bus to go to the field, it was dead silence; not a single person said a word until we got to the stadium because it was so hard to get that out of our minds,” he said. “We understood, if we don’t win this thing, it’s well deserved on the other side.” Curt Schilling and Randy Johnson helped Arizona dominate the first two games at home, outscoring the Yanks by 13 runs to 1 and the series was in danger of becoming a rout. But everything changed for the next three games in New York when the series really came to life. Dellucci says that it took the Diamondbacks an hour to get into Yankee Stadium for Game 3. Security officials had to be sure that there wasn’t a bomb on the bus of the team that was 2-0 up in the World Series. Umpire Dale Scott described the intense security operation as he entered the stadium, passing through newly installed metal detectors and stopping to show identification to a man he’d known for years. Scott told CNN Sports that he passed security personnel every 20 feet until he made his way into the umpire’s room, where he met a man he’d never seen before. It was a Secret Service agent who informed him that he’d be wearing an umpire’s uniform on the field. “He had a gun, he had handcuffs, he had zip ties, he had a taser,” Scott recalled to CNN. “At one point, I said, ‘Could I borrow that taser? I might need that sometime this game.’ “The atmosphere, it was intense,” Scott explained. “They had bomb sniffing dogs, they had a dirty bomb mobile operating facility, they had snipers everywhere.” A famous first pitch When Deborah Tymon had arrived at Yankee Stadium just in time to watch the second plane hit the North Tower of the World Trade Center, she couldn’t have imagined that, three weeks later, she’d be handing the president of the United States the ball for the ceremonial first pitch. But when the moment finally came, she was more concerned with trying to find a catcher who could snag President George W. Bush’s first pitch. The Secret Service wanted to know exactly who’d be out on the field with Bush, and Yankees catcher Jorge Posada had been vetted and cleared with facial recognition. But Posada was in the bullpen preparing for the game, the clock was ticking and Tymon was feeling the pressure. “We have to cue this first pitch, so I didn’t have a choice,” she recalled. “Our backup catcher Todd Greene was sitting on the bench, and I screamed, ‘Greene, Greene, grab your glove, you’ve gotta go!’” “And of course Greene goes running out to home plate and about 45 men talk to their wrists, like, ‘Who is this guy charging home plate?’ I was quite panic-stricken that I’d sent Todd Greene into a den of wolves. I thought I put his life at risk.” Fortunately, he lived to tell the tale, making the most famous catch of his career; it’s an image that he had blown up for his man cave at home. Nobody could have guessed that Bush had the weight of an entire country on his shoulders as he confidently strode out to the mound wearing a New York City Fire Department pullover over his bulletproof vest. He gave a thumbs-up to the crowd and fired a strike over the plate. Dellucci says that he and his teammates were speechless; the only thing anybody said was, “Wow.” For those who didn’t live through that time, in that place, it might be easy to underestimate the extreme levels of anxiety everyone was feeling. The carnage had appeared so suddenly, and it was so devastating, nobody could be sure that it wouldn’t or couldn’t happen again. Tymon’s mom, who was in her mid-eighties, worked in the ticket office at Yankee Stadium, but her daughter had urged her to stay at home that night. She’d been hearing the sirens near the stadium for weeks; she’d seen all the military activity and the helicopters flying around. “You were just waiting for it to happen again, you didn’t think it was one and done,” she recalled. “I said, ‘I’m so afraid, Mom. If anything happens, I can’t get us both out of that building.’” But with just one pitch, Bush managed to convey a sense of strength and hope. “You look up and see security on the roof, you were afraid for him, and when he walked out onto the mound, it was the most peaceful, consoling moment,” she said. “Like, you really believed he was in charge, he was gonna take care of it, and it was so overwhelming that it gave you a peace, that fear you had disappeared. He was in charge and he took that mound with no fear.” The president didn’t stick around for the game, and Dellucci said he felt the mood change as soon as he’d been whisked off the field and left it to the players. “The president left and so did the snipers,” he laughed, “And so now we’re trying to win and we’re sitting ducks out here!” By their own admission, the Yankees hadn’t been playing well that season. Outfielder Shane Spencer told CNN Sports that they didn’t even deserve to be in the World Series. After 9/11, he said they were just going through the motions in batting practice. He still gets emotional thinking about it now because he watched the towers collapse from his home in New Jersey across the Hudson River. “It was such a beautiful day,” he recalled, wiping a tear from his cheek. “It looked fake. We didn’t know what to do. You’re crying all the time, holding hands with firemen and first responders; it was a tough time.” But he says that Bush’s pitch and the energy of the New York crowd jolted them from their daze. “The whole place went crazy, it jump-started everything for us,” he said. “Just a feeling, we got a chance here, we are feeding off them, we fed off the president.” The D-Backs were no match for Roger Clemens’ firepower from the mound that night, and the Yankees got back into the series with a Posada home run and an RBI from Scott Brosius. Mr. November is born But on the next night, Halloween, they found themselves needing little short of a miracle in the bottom of the ninth inning. The Yankees were trailing 3-1 with just one out left. But with a last throw of the dice, Tino Martinez smashed a two-run homer to level the contest, sending the game to extra innings and the World Series into its first November action. The clock dramatically struck midnight during shortstop Derek Jeter’s 10th inning at-bat. At 12:01 a.m. he leveled the series with an extraordinary home run. That’s why they call him “Mr. November.” It was a seemingly impossible comeback by the Yankees, but what happened the next night was unbelievable. Again, the Yankees were two down in the ninth inning, again they were down to their final out, and again they tied it up with a two-run homer – this time from Brosius. Alfonso Soriano then settled the game with an RBI single in the 12th inning, giving New York a 3-2 win and a 3-2 series lead. Those who were in attendance for those games say they’ve never heard Yankee Stadium so loud. An incredible comeback in Phoenix The Yankees might have thought they were heading for a fourth consecutive World Series title, a gift to so many New Yorkers who’d been so impacted by the attacks. But their luck evaporated in the desert, where the Diamondbacks discovered some magic of their own. Johnson muted the pinstripes with a dominant performance in Game 6, and the 15-2 score was one of the most lopsided in World Series history. Now, it was all on the line in a winner-takes-all Game 7. Dellucci told CNN Sports that the Diamondbacks gathered recently for a 25-year reunion, and he said that nobody could remember much about that game until the ninth inning. However, the details of that final inning are indelibly stamped in all their memories. The D-Backs trailed the Yankees 2-1 and New York had Mariano Rivero on the mound; a closer with 23 consecutive postseason saves to his name. Surely, the Yankees were home and dry. But the home team managed to tie up the game, and they loaded the bases in time for that season’s Home Run Derby winner Luis Gonzalez to take the plate. At that moment, Dellucci says he noticed something behind home plate. “There’s a collection of white napkins, and it’s a little mini tornado that’s just kind of swirling,” he said. “We look at each other and say, ‘You know what, they had their magic in New York, and this is a sign, this is our magic happening.’” The narrative seemed poised for the team’s top batter to launch the winning shot into the stands. Instead, he blooped a single just over the infield, allowing the Diamondbacks to clinch the most extraordinary World Series triumph. In a profound moment of national vulnerability, when Americans needed a distraction from the suffering and anxiety, baseball provided it. A seven-game series that went down to the wire, there were two extra-innings games in New York that will be remembered among the most dramatic World Series contests of all time. Dellucci and his teammates had fulfilled their personal dreams and made history as the fastest franchise to win a World Series. But as he looked around the stadium, he understood that he was now a part of something so much bigger. Glancing up into the suites, he made eye contact with the families of the first responders who’d been invited to the game. “You look at them, and you can’t help but smile because they’re smiling at you. You realize it’s much bigger than just the game,” he said. “We’d get phone calls and fan mail, that said, citizens were afraid. They didn’t know what was going to happen next, but by sitting there and watching a baseball game, they were able to return to normalcy for just a little bit,” Dellucci added. “If it had been a blowout, they would have drifted back to what’s next and how terrible this all is. But it was a nail-biter, back and forth, that allowed people to stay engaged and watch every pitch. “For a good three hours, you completely forgot where we were as a country and focused on one of the greatest World Series in the history of baseball.”

articles.title: Shadab Khan’s record-breaking innings gives Pakistan ODI win over England
articles.summary: Pakistan came back from 154-9 to beat England by one wicket, thanks to a historic innings by all-rounder Shadab Khan.
articles.body:
Pakistan had all but lost hope of winning their One-Day International (ODI) cricket match against England when all-rounder Shadab Khan walked onto the pitch to bat and stormed off it with an unlikely come-from-behind win in the bag, in front of a raucous home crowd in Lahore.

The hosts were reduced to 154-9 in the chase of 242 on Sunday, and England were in sight of their first win of the tri-nation series when Shadab and fast bowler Haris Rauf came together for the last-wicket partnership.

From there on, Shadab put on a run-chase masterclass, hitting an unbeaten century to give Pakistan a one-wicket victory and book a spot in the series final.

The 28-year-old launched a surprise counterattack on England, ending up with 113 not out off 96 balls alongside Rauf (7 not out off 19). Shadab and Rauf’s partnership was the highest last-wicket stand in a successful run chase in ODI history.

Earlier in England’s innings, Ben Duckett was the lone batting saviour, scoring 105 off 111 for his fifth ODI century. Once Arafat Minhas dismissed him, England looked hopeless as Shaheen Afridi’s impressive bowling cleaned up their batting lineup.

He took his fourth wicket (4-46) to remove Henry Crocombe. England’s last-wicket pair added 39 to post a below-par total of 241 all out from 46.4 overs.

England then decimated Pakistan’s top order as Jamie Overton (3-43) and Liam Dawson (2-19) removed Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Babar Azam and Saad Baig cheaply.

The hosts ultimately slumped to 154-9, having been 74-3. By this point, England had all but secured victory as the home crowd began leaving Gaddafi Stadium after the ninth wicket fell.

Shadab stepped up to flip the script and produce the batting performance of a lifetime when he prised victory away from England, particularly after his leg-before-wicket dismissal was overturned on review.

“I dedicate this win to the two most wonderful women in my life: my mother & my wife,” Shadab wrote on social media following the victory.

“Special mention for [Haris Rauf], we win only as a team and he showed that today in the partnership. Thank you to my entire team.”

The victory went some way towards restoring faith among Pakistani cricket fans, who have endured months of dismal performances at global tournaments, as well as bilateral series.

It was “an innings to remember”, as former Pakistani cricketer Mohammad Hafeez put it, while teammate Imad Wasim praised Shadab for handling the extreme pressure.

“That was a sensational innings by Shadab Khan,” Sri Lanka’s veteran cricketer Angelo Mathews wrote on X. “Won it for Pakistan out of nowhere.”

Barbadian wicketkeeper-batsman Shai Hope called the match “absolute cinema” while former West Indies cricketer Daren Sammy termed it “another thriller”, referring to Sri Lanka’s thrashing of England on Thursday when they recorded the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history.

Praise and memes kept pouring in on social media as one user joked about making a documentary of the game, while others reiterated the need for more trilateral series in ODI format.

Speaking after the match, Pakistan’s captain Afridi said he was pleased with the team’s overall performance, especially the way Shadab and Haris finished the game.

“We thought we had a lot of variation in the team, so that’s why we brought Shadab in,” the fast bowler said.

“We need top-order runs; we’re struggling. I hope in the next few games we’ll bring that energy.

“I think tonight we’ll be celebrating; tomorrow back to normal.”

English cricket commentator Nasser Hussain praised Pakistan’s “incredible run chase” as he credited Shadab’s change of intent in the heat of the moment.

“Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf; that partnership, you had to be really switched on and smart how you played it,” Hussain said on Sky Sports.

“The moment they changed intent, the moment Shadab said ‘right we’ve gone one way, it’s gone nowhere, we’re going to play our shots’, there’s a lesson to be learnt,” Hussain said, referring to the previous game when England were put under pressure.

“Brilliant change of intent from Shadab Khan; that game had gone from them. Took one individual backed up by Haris Rauf to bring it back.”

Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf echoed a similar sentiment.

“Superb display of positive intent! Fearless, aggressive and full of belief. Take a bow,” he wrote on X.

Speaking alongside Hussain, retired English cricketer Chris Woakes agreed on Shadab’s spectacular performance: “A hundred not out at number eight is pretty special!”
