articles.title: Manchester United crisis: What are the top five problems facing the club?
articles.summary: Manchester United hit a new low on Sunday with a home loss to Bournemouth. So, how can they solve their issues?
articles.body:
Manchester United are facing the greatest crisis in the Premier League club’s history.

Their worst start to a league season in 40 years was extended with a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday.

It threw not only the manager’s future into doubt , but every member of the ownership, senior management and playing squad as a whole.

United fans do not turn on their managers or players. That changed on Sunday when fans cheered off Michael Carrick and then booed off the players.

The message is clear: United fans are not prepared to take any more – and that goes from the top to the bottom of the first-team set-up and those who recruited them.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at the problems plaguing the club:

Do Man United need a striker more than a new manager?

Since Cristiano Ronaldo left United in November 2022 after his second stint at Old Trafford, the side has struggled for a regular goalscorer.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic was a short-term fix before Ronaldo’s return, while Romelu Lukaku was unable to turn a reputation into returns.

Danish striker Rasmus Hojlund was recruited as United’s answer to Manchester City’s Erling Haaland, but a lack of goals saw the youngster shipped back to Italy.

Enter the big-money arrival of Serbian international Benjamin Sesko in the summer of 2025. The 23-year-old has impressed in patches, but injuries have also taken their toll, and his absence in United’s woeful start to the season has been glaring.

United have tried Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo as strikers, but both are naturally wide players who thrive on running at defenders.

Then came the false nine, with Bruno Fernandes handed a role perfected by Lionel Messi at Barcelona.

Too often in Fernandes’s case, however, the Portuguese playmaker found himself with his back to goal and unable to pull the strings of the runners around him.

Having won the Professional Footballers’ Association’s Player of the Year award on the back of breaking the Premier League record for the number of assists in a season, the role took his greatest ability away from him.

Eight players sit above United’s leading scorer – Mbeumo, with four goals – in the Premier League’s scoring chart this season; all of them would walk into the United side.

United’s top brass: The Glazers, Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada

The Glazer family bought into Manchester United in 2005, long before Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013. However, it is now believed that English football’s most successful manager and then-CEO David Gill were masking the problems brought by the US family’s ownership.

United’s signings in the last 13 years – 75 in total – have been nothing short of disastrous. Fernandes is perhaps the only player who would come close to breaking into one of the Ferguson sides during the spell between his first league title in 1993 and his last, when he finally hung up his hairdryer.

Ed Woodward was the Glazers’ appointed CEO until 2022, and was lambasted by fans for the endless run of failed signings and sacked managers.

The duo currently responsible for player recruitment, CEO Omar Berrada and the technical director, are the latest pairing to receive the wrath of the Old Trafford support, and, it seems, the dressing room.

Defender Lisandro Martinez, who helped Argentina reach the 2026 World Cup final , took aim at Wilcox in particular after United’s defeat at Atletico Madrid when he criticised the lack of investment in the squad in the summer.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s INEOS Group invested heavily in United two years ago. The move led to controversial off-field cuts, and with them came grand plans for the club’s training ground and proposals to rebuild Old Trafford .

The return so far has been minimal, and Ratcliffe and INEOS are regarded in the same light as the Glazers – an unwanted relative at each family gathering.

Manager vs star player: Carrick vs Fernandes

Whoever is in charge of United through the end of the season and beyond will have one big question to answer: Does Fernandes have a future at the club after openly criticising Carrick?

The Portuguese was booed off after the defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday, even though he did not set foot on the field, punishment for his decision to call out Carrick’s tactics after Wednesday’s defeat in Como.

At 32, Fernandes is closer to the end of his career than to the start, but he remains United’s standout performer. When he ticks, so do United. When he does not, United appear to be relegation fodder.

His esteem among the fans is based on the belief that he has shouldered the club since his 2020 arrival; even with the brief return of Ronaldo, Fernandes was still the star of the show.

They have, however, considered cashing in on the Portuguese playmaker, with the Saudi Pro League prepared to break the bank to lure him away.

Galatasaray were also known to be another suitor this summer. Fernandes, in response, made no secret of his disappointment in the club’s openness to selling him – something both parties may now consider inevitable.

To buy a left-back – or be left behind the rest?

One of the biggest surprises in the summer, alongside failing to reinforce their options alongside Sesko in attack, was the failure to bring in a left-back. Indeed, it is believed the lack of depth in that position in particular is what led to Martinez blasting the club hierarchy .

Lewis Hall of Newcastle United was heavily linked with a move throughout the summer, and on the final day of the transfer window it was assumed the deal would be done, given no other player was acquired in that role.

Man United’s identity: Press, sit deep or ‘attack, attack, attack’

The famous United chant of “attack, attack, attack” was the foundation of the club. It undoubtedly led to their rise to become the world’s number one club – under Matt Busby with his babes in the 1950s, then his rebuilt giants led by George Best and Bobby Charlton, then the hallmark of Ferguson’s team to the very last kick of so many games.

Fernandes slammed Carrick for not pressing Como in the Champions League and allowing a relative minnow at that level to dictate the play. Sitting deep has never been the United way, and Jose Mourinho – now revelling again in his second stint at Real Madrid – faced a player revolt even though the United fans remained faithful.

Louis van Gaal came with his own “philosophy” of passing the opposition to death – denying a club that have always been famed for flying wingers the chance to live up to their reputation. Again, the players – reportedly led by Wayne Rooney and Carrick – were not happy with the sideways movements.

Ruben Amorim’s 3-4-3 formation appeared to leave the players more baffled than anyone else, while Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Carrick – both prodigies of Ferguson – managed to open up a free-flowing style akin to that of their old manager and mentor. Neither was able to maintain a run of form to hold on to the position.

Ralf Rangnick, now the national team coach of Austria, said the club as a whole required “open-heart surgery”.

Gary Neville went a step further on Sky Sports on Sunday, alleging levels of unprofessionalism from certain members of the squad.

“There are a few of them that are not that professional,” the former United and England defender said.

What is for sure is that United on the field need a style, a personality and a commitment to the cause that first and foremost will reconnect a disjointed group with one of the most patient and loyal supports in the world.

As things stand, the locals are beyond restless, and a revolution may not only be required; it may well be demanded in no uncertain terms in the coming weeks and months.

articles.title: Juan Lebrón tiende la mano a Ale Galán para jugar juntos en el Mundial: "Lo haría todos los días"
articles.standfirst: El gaditano habló sobre la posibilidad de reunirse con su excompañero en Doha
articles.summary: El gaditano habló sobre la posibilidad de reunirse con su excompañero en Doha
articles.body: El Mundial de pádel está a la vuelta de la esquina. España y Argentina se disputarán un nuevo campeonato del mundo en Doha del 2 al 7 de noviembre, y en el plano del combinado nacional español muchos debates se centran en si Lebrón y Galán deberían volver a reunirse en pista. Juanjo Gutiérrez, seleccionador, ya dijo en MARCA hace un mes que ambos jugarán juntos, aunque la duda se centra en si lo harán en la eliminatoria definitiva o si será durante la semana. Sobre esto, Lebrón ha sido contundente en rueda de prensa durante el Major de Kuwait: "Jugaría con quien haga falta. España y la selección están por encima de todos". Centrándose en concreto con Galán, afirmó que "la relación no es la mejor" pero reflexionó sobre el momento que viven ambos. "Jugaría con Ale todos los días del Mundial si hiciese falta, está a un nivel altísimo y obviamente lo principal es que gane España un nuevo Mundial", explicó el 'Lobo'. El gaditano buscará un nuevo título Mundial e incidió en que está abierto a jugar con el compañero que sea, ya fuese Paquito, Aimar o el propio Galán, abogando por la unión de un equipo que quiere evitar el tercer triunfo seguido albiceleste.

articles.title: Dynamic duo: Shaker's Puls twins choose Bryant University for college lacrosse
articles.summary: After leading Shaker girls' lacrosse to a Section 2 Class A title, standout juniors Kiera and Kinley Puls have made their college choice.
articles.body:
Kiera and Kinley Puls were sought after individually and as a pair during their college lacrosse recruitment. In the end, the twin sisters, who have excelled for two seasons competing side by side at Shaker, decided that staying together at the collegiate level was the right move.

The sister tandem has given Bryant University coach Eileen Ferry their oral commitments to compete for the Bulldogs of the America East Conference. Ferry, the 2025 America East Coach of the Year, led Bryant to regular season titles in 2025 and 2026.

"Most of the schools reached out to both of us to come together, but some didn't," said Kiera Puls, a 2026 Times Union first-team all-star as a draw specialist who won 239 times. "When we tried to figure out what was best, we both thought it was Bryant."

"I initially had my mind set that I wanted to go south," Kinley Puls said. "(Kiera) liked being up here and I thought, 'What are we going to do without each other?' We have always been together."

Ferry made the offer to both twins. They took a couple of days to ultimately decide to compete together for the Bulldogs.

"Having that chemistry already and knowing someone so well, Coach Ferry was talking about having both of us and how well we would fit in together," Kiera Puls said.

Kinley Puls said there were a few days right before the sisters decided to stay together where they pondered the possibility of being apart in college, but she added, "We were riding in the car and looked at each other and said, 'We're going to Bryant, right?' … As we went on other visits, nothing compared to Bryant. Coach Ferry and all of the coaches had everything set up and were so much more organized than everyone else. I realized it was the best fit for me."

"They are going to do an incredible job in college," Shaker coach Joe Pollicino said. "What they have been able to do during their first two years on the varsity has been very impressive. I am interested to see what they are going to do going forward with the other (12) players we have coming back."

Shaker, with a 2026 squad featuring 11 sophomores paced by the Puls' sisters, captured its first sectional title in 10 years by defeating Shenendehowa in the Section 2 Class A championship and finished 16-4 overall.

"What they have done is impressive," Pollicino said of the twins. "The two of them had a great year for us last year, helping lead us to heights I don't think we would have gotten to without them. Kiera at the draw got us a lot of extra possessions, which was important. Kinley, who, for us being in a low lefty spot, enhanced the offense and created so many opportunities for Libby (Gialanella) and Tessa (Carroll). That was great as well."

"Playing against so many amazing girls and such high-level competition has really helped me improve," said Kiera Puls, "especially taking the draw against some tough girls definitely helped me."

Kiera Puls tallied 26 goals and 44 assists as a sophomore, while Kinley Puls has already surpassed 150 career points in two years on the varsity. The juniors are looking forward to the upcoming season and what they can accomplish at Shaker.

"It is such a relief now," said Kinley Puls, "to just be able to play and not worry about who is watching."

articles.summary: Mike and Dan recap the Islanders’ up-and-down week, look ahead to a scary schedule and bring receipts to an epic Master Sens Theatre. The Islanders won one f...
articles.body:
Mike and Dan recap the Islanders' up-and-down week, look ahead to a scary schedule and bring receipts to an epic Master Sens Theatre.

The Islanders won one fun game, lost a game in overtime they were the better team in and then lost to a contender that overmatched them by a lot. With four regulars out of the lineup, their already pop gun offense and frequent missed opportunities looked even worse. They also have some games coming up in places they never win, making the mediocre results they got much more dire. There were things to like, like electric Matthew Schaefer goals, players who needed it cashing in and Pete DeBoer's structure still being executed well. But the reality of what this team is is settling in, and the good feelings from last week are fading.

We also discuss the team's unforced error of trying to "explain" Mat Barzal's absence and when – or if – he'll be back in the lineup. This also ties back to early season attendance issues and the lingering UBS Arena parking problem the organization doesn't seem to want to address. It would be great to make people feel good again with some wins in unlikely places and at home on Halloween. But the Magic 8 Ball isn't coming up in their favor.

In the second half, we also discuss the Connor Hellebyuck trade to New Jersey and the Metro Division before diving into an operatic Master Sens Theatre about the already legendary Brady Tkachuk return game. Everyone loves how Ottawa fans brutalized their former captain all game long, which is a far cry from how they treated Islanders fans who did the same thing to their traitorous returning captain back in 2019. But don't take our word for it; we've got the tweets, articles and quotes to prove what we know was true.

articles.title: Broncos injuries: WR Jaylen Waddle, DL Zach Allen injured vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle and DE Zach Allen left Sunday's game with injuries in the fourth quarter.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos secured their first two-score win of the season on Sunday with a 30-16 victory over the Arizona Cardinals , but the win did come at a cost.

Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle ( chest ) and defensive lineman Zach Allen ( appeared to be hamstring ) both went down with injuries in the fourth quarter. Waddle suffered his injury after falling on his own fumble on an end-around . After the game, coach Sean Payton called it a " dumb reverse call ." Payton apologized for the "awful" call in his post-game press conference.

Waddle initially stayed down on the field before walking to the sideline and then into the locker room. He was previously limited in two days of practice last week with a chest injury. Denver announced Waddle as questionable to return, but he did not return to Sunday's game after totaling four catches for 48 yards prior to the injury.

Allen also went down in the fourth quarter and appeared to be favoring his right hamstring. After a visit to the team's blue medical tent, Allen was spotted standing on the sideline without his helmet for the end of the game. Allen went to the podium for a post-game press conference after the win and said, "Yeah, I'll be fine. Yeah, I'll be good," when asked about his injury.

Elsewhere on the injury front, cornerback Pat Surtain ( ankle ) missed his third straight game on Sunday and safety Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ) sat out his second consecutive game. After the win, Surtain said, "Not really," when asked by the Denver Gazette 's Chris Tomasson if he was close to playing in Arizona. When asked if he'll play against the Chiefs on Sunday, Surtain said, "Possibly." Denver's first injury report of the week will come out on Wednesday.

articles.title: With six straight losses, Northwestern Women’s Soccer looks to be a different team than they started the season with. Anya Weerapana reflects.
articles.summary: Six straight losses in the Big Ten see Northwestern with its lowest-winning record since 2019.
articles.body:
As the twilight of this column begins to set in, it is time to look back to the very beginning of this season in mid-August and reflect on the journey that Northwestern Women's Soccer has taken us on.

Back then, Northwestern had a young roster eager to take on top competition. The Wildcats putting one past Virginia on Aug. 12 in a game they were outclassed felt like a sign of their future goal-scoring capabilities under pressure.

Flash forward two months and five days, and Northwestern has dropped two consecutive games to bottom-of-Big-Ten competition Maryland and USC in a stretch of games that were critical to its making the Big Ten Tournament. The team now sits at 5-10-3, its lowest winning season since 2019.

A pair of losses against Illinois on Thursday and Purdue on Sunday has brought Northwestern's losing streak to six.

I called this column "reflections" because I wanted to look back at the team's season. Like a mirror, however, we should also see the realities of what we look back on without any sort of embellishment or post-hoc sugarcoating.

The worst part about this year was that nearly everything that went wrong was out of the Wildcats' control. Keira Kemmerley, then Kennedy Roesch, then Ava Goodin ended up injured and done for the season; Nyamma Nelson and Megan Norkett were suspended for a game each after receiving red cards. Every single tactical switch on head coach Michael Moynihan's part felt it was less out of his own volition and more out of actual necessity.

Just five players — including Kate Hennen and CJ Roy, who normally have not gotten starts this season — carried over from the starting lineup against Virginia in Northwestern's most recent matchup against Purdue. That fact alone shows how much turnover Northwestern has had to deal with all year.

Change, however, can be a good thing. We saw a handful of stars break out in the first-year recruiting class: Elle Phillips, Gwen Zimmerman, Naomi Lofthouse and Camryn Freeman, who surged forward in the last third of the season with five goals to become the team's out-and-out goalscorer. We saw a handful of returners re-establish their marks: Alex Fallon and Holland Carey, both returning from injury, made a significant impact on and off the field for this program.

Though we don't know what Northwestern's recruiting class is going to look like next year, one can hope that the recent success Moynihan has had picking players up from top Midwestern clubs will translate for the third year in a row. Northwestern's injuries this season have meant that this year's freshman class has had a level of autonomy in their play one could only dream of, and that will surely set them up for success on the collegiate level next year. One year older, one year wiser, as they say.

With Northwestern being squarely out of contention for the Big Ten Tournament this season, it has unsuccessfully managed to replicate last year's on-paper accomplishments. But I'd like to make the argument that this season has shown the team how flexible it can be, how it can cultivate goalscorers off its bench and how it can move around formations from a three-back to a four-back and do so with a backup goalkeeper in net.

This year has been the year of lessons for the Wildcats. And while that isn't their fault, their season is so much more than their record. Because, as this year has shown us thanks to Northwestern Lacrosse, Field Hockey and Football, any comeback is possible — whether that's physical or metaphorical.

articles.title: Question Time: Which Jays Player Surprised You By Being Better Than You Expected?
articles.summary: I’m traveling today, so won’t be posting. And, there isn’t much for Jays news today. So let’s have a question: Which Jays player surprised you by being much...
articles.body:
I'm traveling today, so won't be posting. And, there isn't much for Jays news today.

So let's have a question: Which Jays player surprised you by being much better than you expected?

For me? Marco Estrada would be the obvious choice. When we traded Adam Lind for him, I was disappointed with the return. Estrada played five seasons with the Brewers and posted a 23-25 record with a 4.11 ERA in 159 games, including 70 starts. He couldn't hold a spot in the starting rotation and ended up in the bullpen as middle relief.

Lind had hit 146 home runs in 9 seasons with us, topping out at 35 in 2009. He became a platoon player when he couldn't hit lefties, but he still had a lot of power, and power is useful.

Estrada played four seasons with the Jays, posting a 4.25 ERA and a 9.6 bWAR, and he saved his best starts for the playoffs, with a 2.16 ERA in 6 starts and 41.2 playoff innings. He took two no-hitters into the ninth.

Lind played one season with the Brewers. It was a good one: .277/.360/.460 with 20 home runs in 149 games. Then the Brewers traded him to the Mariners, where he had a -0.3 bWAR in 126 games, with 20 home runs and a .239/.286/.431 batting line. From there, he went to the Nationals for one good season, his last in the majors. He spent the next couple of years in the minor leagues with the Yankees and Red Sox.

The Jays saw something in Estrada and helped him become a very good starting pitcher.

articles.title: England handed Fin Smith injury worry ahead of autumn Tests
articles.summary: Charlie Atkinson has been called up as cover for England’s first-choice fly half
articles.body:
England have been handed a potential blow ahead of their Nations Championship Tests with Fin Smith facing further assessment on a calf injury.

Smith was named as part of a 36-man training squad by head coach Steve Borthwick on Sunday, but will not train this week and instead begin his rehabilitation in camp having featured in Northampton's defeat to Leicester on Saturday.

Borthwick is expected to provide an update on the extent of the injury to his first-choice fly half on Tuesday, with Gloucester's Charlie Atkinson called up as cover.

Smith has started England's last five Tests after usurping George Ford at No 10 during the Six Nations, and had been expected to start their November opener against Australia in less than a fortnight.

While it is hoped he will be fit, any possible absence would be significant ahead of a busy international period that also includes games against Japan and New Zealand, and a fixture on the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium.

Borthwick is also without centre Seb Atkinson and wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, who are rehabbing knee and hamstring injuries respectively, this week, while Benhard Janse van Rensburg was not included in his squad having suffered a head injury earlier this month playing for Bristol.

His fly half options remain strong, though, with Marcus Smith in excellent recent form for Harlequins and veteran Ford highly valued for his experience and leadership within the group. Atkinson has impressed, meanwhile, for Prem table-toppers Gloucester following a strong campaign last season.

articles.title: Bayern's Eberl: We don't really understand what we achieved this week
articles.summary: Bayern Munich board member for sport Max Eberl said he doesn't think the people in the club "really understand what we've achieved this week" as the Bavarian...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich board member for sport Max Eberl said he doesn't think the people in the club "really understand what we've achieved this week" as the Bavarians overcame the collapse of coach Vincent Kompany and the additional absence of key players with a 3-1 triumph at Freiburg on Sunday.

"I don't think we really understand what we've achieved this week with all the hurdles we've had to overcome. What the team and we as a group have done with the coaching staff is extraordinary," Eberl said.

"The win means three points, but it was a bigger win than just three points. Obviously we've got problems at the moment, but we have our squad and are really happy."

Kompany collapsed while watching a training session of Bayern's reserve team. He had been suffering from a virus in previous days but the reason for the collapse is not known.

Other Bayern absentees in Freiburg apart from Kompany were Joshua Kimmich due to a family bereavement as well as Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala, Aleksandar Pavlović, Luis Díaz and Kim Minjae for injury reasons.

"It was clear to everyone that this game marked the end of a very, very difficult week, both physically and mentally," goalkeeper Jonas Urbig said.

Urbig deputized once again for Neuer and made a crucial save at the end of the game when Bayern were leading 2-1 to deny Freiburg the equalizer.

With the three points, Bayern moved back into first place on goal difference over Borussia Dortmund ahead of the two sides' table-topper showdown on Saturday in Munich.

"We have a good cohesion, everyone supports everyone, no matter how difficult the situation is and what each individual is going through. We stand together, not only this week, but especially this week," Urbig said.

There were some good news for Bayern on Monday as defender Kim and midfielder Pavlović trained individually with the ball. The players who featured in the win against Freiburg, meanwhile, completed a recovery session.

Bayern will hope for more good news later as star striker Harry Kane is among the favourites to win the Ballon D'Or award. Eberl will miss the ceremony and won't travel to London because of a cold.

articles.title: Raiders Week 8: Meet the Jets
articles.summary: Can Raiders win their third straight game against the Jets
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are preparing to play their eighth regular-season game of the year, their fourth on the road, at the New York Jets on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 10 a.m. PT.

The Jets are 2-5 after a home 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. It was the Dolphins' first win of the season:

This will be only the third meeting between these two AFC opponents, that have struggled in recent seasons, this decade. The Raiders beat the Jets 16-12 on November 12, 2023 (early in the Antonio Peirce interim coaching days). This will be the Raiders' first trip to New York since their inprobable last second win when Derek Carr hit Henry Ruggs in December, 2020, to pull of an inprobabale victory. Now, Las Vegas is looking for three straight wins over the Jets.

articles.title: Blue Jays predicted to sign $85M former Silver Slugger finalist to boost World Series hopes
articles.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays will enter 2027 with a massive chip on their should. A move to get this high caliber of a bat in free agency would revive World Series...
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays finished the season without making the playoffs after a magical 2025 campaign. Injuries and other factors kept them from finding their rhythm throughout the season.

The team is hungry to do better in 2027, and it all starts with free agency. The Blue Jays were aggressive last winter, and they should be this winter, too.

"After falling inches short of a World Series ring in 2025, the Toronto Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins was extremely aggressive in the offseason as he was able to acquire Dylan Cease, Spencer Miles, Tyler Rogers, and Kazuma Okamoto in a short span of time. But the Blue Jays fell far short in their quest for redemption, finishing last in the AL East and below .500, and missing the playoffs altogether," SI's Maddy Dickens wrote.

There are already rumors swirling that the Blue Jays are very interested in Chicago Cubs right fielder Seiya Suzuki.

"The Blue Jays didn't make the playoffs this year, so they are already in offseason mode. Mitch Bannon of The Athletic reports that the Jays are expected to pursue outfielder Seiya Suzuki when he hits free agency about a month from now," MLB Trade Rumors' Darragh McDonald wrote.

Dickens believes Toronto should sign Suzuki to help revive its World Series hopes.

"So, who should general manager Ross Atkins be looking at? Well, the best answer would be the right-handed Seiya Suzuki, who is on an expiring deal with the Chicago Cubs. One of the best aspects of Suzuki's game is that he has pop in the bat, which is something that the Jays were severely lacking this season, as only Kazuma Okamoto was able to hit more than 15 bombs. This season, Suzuki finished the year with 26 home runs and 31 doubles to complement 86 runners driven home as well as 81 drawn walks," Dickens wrote.

Suzuki could give the Blue Jays what they need in a player, as he has a powerful bat and an absolute cannon for an arm. Toronto can add talent this offseason and prove that its disappointing 2026 campaign was a fluke.

Suzuki is finishing his $85 million contract with the Cubs. The former Silver Slugger finalist would provide a valuable bat in the lineup, an area where Toronto struggled at times this season.

articles.title: Missouri State defensive end Kellen Lindstrom out for season
articles.summary: Missouri State defensive end and Glendale alum Kellen Lindstrom will miss the remainder of the season due to an upcoming surgery.
articles.body:
SPRINGFIELD — Missouri State (2-5, 1-2 in CUSA) will be without local standout Kellen Lindstrom for the rest of the season, including Tuesday's game against Sam Houston.

Head coach Casey Woods confirmed the news to Springfield radio's ESPN the Jock on Monday, Oct. 26.

"He's going to have a season-ending surgery coming up," Woods said. "I hate that for him, but we've got to continue to fight."

Missouri State football hosts Kennesaw State in Conference USA clash

The Glendale alum has been a mainstay across the Bears' defensive line this season. He has nine tackles, including one tackle for a loss. He missed the Kennesaw State game with an injury, but he did feature in the Bears' latest game against Delaware.

Lindstrom transferred to Missouri State this season after two years at Tennessee. At Glendale, he was an all-state player and one of the best in the Springfield area in 2023.

Missouri State hosts Sam Houston at 7 p.m. on Tuesday, Oct. 27 at Plaster Stadium.

articles.title: The week ahead: Penguins get much-needed schedule rest, and some potential returns
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins have some days off this week and could get some players back in the lineup very soon.
articles.body:
Given the way the four-game Western road trip went, and given the number of players that missed games this week due to illness or injury, it is really easy to be impressed with the way the Penguins handled this past week's worth of games.

But then the Penguins returned home for Thursday's game against the Florida Panthers, and Saturday's game against the Nashville Predators, and played what might have been their two best back-to-back games of the season. I know, Florida presented a scheduling advantage due to the Panthers' travel and a back-to-back situation, and Nashville isn't really a contender. But the Penguins had been in Florida's shoes multiple times this season and nobody felt sympathy for them, and while Nashville isn't a contender, the Predators came back on Sunday and absolutely steamrolled the Colorado Avalanche.

So, what I'm saying is, take the points where you get them.

Even better than the wins is just the reality that the Penguins played two really good, really clean games. They were the better team in both games, even if they trailed for a good portion of the Nashville game. Given the way they played it would have been incredibly frustrating to not get at least a point out of that game.

Now they have a four-day break before their next game on Thursday night when they get a quick rematch with Utah, this time at home.

We already know what Utah is capable of, and that's a really good hockey team that is, again, going to present a formidable challenge. They are fast, deep, and one of the best offensive teams in the league. They enter the week sixth in the NHL in goals per game (3.83) and still have the No. 1 power play unit in the league (38.1 percent). For as much as the Penguins struggled in the first meeting, they still put together a strong third period that put them into a position where they were a highlight reel, last-second save away from actually tying the game. It did not produce a point, but it did at least set some wheels in motion to maybe build some momentum for the two games that followed.

After hosting Utah on Thursday, the Penguins travel to Montreal on Saturday to play the Canadiens for the second time this season.

The Penguins won the first meeting in a wild overtime game in the second game of the season. It was a game that saw the Penguins dominate early, and then experience one of their biggest flaws from 2025-26 and let a three-goal third period lead slip away. They were able to salvage it with a Tommy Novak overtime goal.

After losing three of their first four games of the season, Montreal has responded by going 5-1-1 in the past seven games.

Saturday's game will be its first game back home after a long road trip, while the Canadiens are also currently without top center Nick Suzuki, who will be sidelined for several weeks. That takes a big player away from them (arguably their best player), and puts a big dent in their already questionable center depth, but the rest of the roster has enough talent that will still make Montreal a tough, tough opponent.

In terms of opponents, the Penguins are still in the middle of a brutal stretch, which not only continues this week, but also into next week with home games against the Vegas Golden Knights and Boston Bruins.

While the opponents are still tough, the days off this week come at a great time. Not only due to the injuries, but also the fact the Penguins have played a lot of hockey with a lot of travel in a short period of time.

What is going to be really interesting to watch this week is what the Penguins do when some of these players start coming back.

Evgeni Malkin and Egor Chinakhov are probably going to be returning.

That is going to force some people back out of the lineup. Probably Rutger McGroarty. Perhaps Avery Hayes. I would not be opposed to taking Andrei Kuzmenko out of the lineup right now.

The two players I do NOT want to see come out of the lineup are Ville Koivunen and Hendrix Lapierre. Koivunen looks like a player that is starting to figure things out and get the confidence he had been lacking a year ago. He is not only producing more, he just looks like a different player. He does not look as perpetually frustrated as he did a year ago. The puck is coming off his stick quicker. The playmaking and passing has been sensational. He and Lapierre also seem to have something cooking with one another. In 45 minutes of 5-on-5 ice-time together the Penguins are outscoring teams 5-0 with them on the ice, while also having a better than 80 percent expected goal and scoring chance share. It is a small sample size, and it has come with some favorable offensive zone starts, but they are feasting on it right now. I want to see what they can keep doing.

That is going to be the big dilemma for Dan Muse, because not only are they playing well, the "fourth" line of Connor Dewar, Elmer Soderblom and Nick Robertson has also been really, really good. I also put "fourth" line in quotes because even though they are listed as fourth on the depth chart, the Penguins are balancing their ice-time so much that it does not really matter what anybody's designation is. They also played the third-most minutes on Saturday.

The other big question: Will we see Sergei Murashov in goal this week?

Arturs Silovs has started three games in a row, and played quite well in the past two games, while Murashov has struggled early on. We should not be surprised that Murashov is having some growing pains, and he did not respond well in his most recent start after the game in Chicago. He is going to get back in there at some point, and there is still good reason to believe he will play better than he has, but I wonder how long Muse will keep riding the hot hand (such as it is after two games). You want to see Murashov play, but after the past two games Silovs played it would be tough to take him out right now. At least as it relates to Thursday's game.

Interesting week ahead with two tough games and some big lineup decisions. Winning Thursday's game would be a good start, and then see if you can get at least a point out of Montreal. Reasonable goal.

articles.title: Big Ten Football Power Rankings: Is anyone good?
articles.summary: Indiana looked horrible in a win while Iowa, USC, Oregon, and Michigan all suffered ugly defeats. Here are our latest Big Ten Football Power Rankings:
articles.body:
The craziness of the Big Ten season didn't stop in Week 8 as both Michigan and Oregon lost again. On top of that, Minnesota righted the ship and Wisconsin stormed the field after a huge win over Lincoln Riley and USC. At this point its fair to ask if anyone in the conference is good this season as no can seem to sustain winning outside of Indiana who hasn't looked impressive while doing so.

With that being said, we still have a job to do. Heading into Week 9 here are our Big Ten Power Rankings:

10. Oregon Ducks: 4-3, Lost to Illinois 10-21, LW: 7

I really didn't want to put anyone at No. 10 because none of the bottom nine teams in the conference deserve it. Oregon gets it by default because the advanced metrics like SP+ and ESPN's Resume FPI like the Ducks better than anyone else, even though Oregon's offense has been gross to watch.

9. Minnesota Golden Gophers: 5-2, Def. Iowa 13-10, LW: 10

P.J. Fleck's squad bounced back after their bad loss to Purdue with a solid win over a then-ranked Iowa team. Minnesota has arguably the toughest remaining strength of schedule in the Big Ten with Indiana, UCLA, Northwestern, and Wisconsin still on the schedule, but so far so good for Minnesota.

8. USC Trojans: 6-2, Lost to Wisconsin 7-24, LW: 6

Lincoln Riley's seat is starting to warm up again following a disastrous loss in Madison. USC gained 241 yards throughout the game with 258 passing yards. Yes, you read that right. USC had -17 yards rushing. How is that even possible? USC's CFP hopes are dwindling fast.

7. Iowa Hawkeyes: 5-2, Lost to Minnesota 10-13, LW: 4

Just when Iowa seemed to have it all figured out, they lost an absolute clunker to Minnesota. Prior to this past week, Iowa was 5-1 with their one loss being to Ohio State. The Hawkeyes were starting to have dark-horse CFP aspirations. While it's still not entirely off the table, the Hawkeyes made it significantly more difficult for themselves. Make no mistake, this was a season-defining loss for Iowa.

6. Nebraska Cornhuskers: 5-2, On bye, LW: 8

Nebraska didn't play on Saturday but thanks to losses by USC, Iowa, and Oregon they move up two spots to No. 6.

5. Wisconsin Badgers: 5-2, Def. USC 24-7, LW: 9

Wisconsin picked up arguably the most surprising result of the weekend with a somewhat easy win over Lincoln Riley and USC. After nearly being fired in the offseason, Luke Fickell has finally turned things around in Madison despite not having a passing game. As much of a feel-good story as Wisconsin is, the fact that we can justify having the Badgers fifth shows how down the Big Ten is this season.

4. Northwestern Wildcats: 6-1, Def. Rutgers 42-14, LW: 6

While beating Rutgers isn't impressive in and of itself, Northwestern's continued offensive prowess certainly is. Offensive coordinator Chip Kelly is looking like one of the greatest hires of the offseason following an underwhelming stint at Ohio State. The Wildcats travel to Oregon on Halloween in a game that I had sharpied in as an Oregon win before the season but now I might be leaning towards the Wildcats. Crazy times we live in.

3. Indiana Hoosiers: 7-1, Def. Michigan 13-6, LW: 2

Indiana won a tough, road battle at the largest stadium in America. So why drop them down a spot in the power rankings? It's simple. Josh Hoover looked like a shell of himself, going 8-for-18 for 81 yards and an interception. The Hoosiers didn't complete a pass in the second half. Fortunately for them, Michigan's offense was even worse. Indiana is still likely to make the CFP, but they look significantly worse than they were last year.

2. UCLA Bruins: 7-0, Def. Michigan State 28-10, Last Week: 3

Is it controversial to flip flop Indiana and UCLA despite both winning this past weekend? Maybe. However, the Bruins deserve all their flowers as they have yet to lose despite no preseason expectations whatsoever. Even without Nico, UCLA has done very well with Ty Dieffenbach under center. Running back Anthony Woods ran for 112 yards and a touchdown against a very bad Michigan State defense.

1. Ohio State Buckeyes: 6-1, On bye, LW: 1

The Buckeyes were a big winner in college football this week as they didn't lose. In a season full of carnage, being on bye is a major advantage.

articles.title: Vote for the All-USA Vermont Boys Athlete of the Week powered by Delta Dental
articles.summary: People who love Vermont high school sports can vote through 9 p.m. Thursday for the boys Athlete of the Week presented by Delta Dental.
articles.body:
Welcome to the eighth installment of the 2026 fall season for the Delta Dental All-USA Vermont Athletes of the Week voting by high school sports fans.

This week, and every week during the sports season, members of the public may vote for a top girls athlete and a top boys athlete. And since last year, we added to the list of weekly nominees: There are now two stories, one for girls and one for boys, with more athletes on each ballot.

All voting is through the ballots at burlingtonfreepress.com. We will not accept votes through email or through social media. To vote, click on the name of the person you want to select and refresh the page after each time you vote to be able to vote as often as you'd like.

Voting began Monday, Oct. 26 and continues through 9 p.m. Thursday, Oct. 29.

The winners will be announced in a story published at burlingtonfreepress.com on Friday, Oct. 30.

May I nominate a deserving athlete for a future ballot?

Yes. Please nominate a Vermont high school athlete by sending an email to sports@burlingtonfreepress.com (Subject Line: Athletes of the Week nomination). Additionally, please include the athlete's school, sport and any relevant details from that week's games in the email.

Hunter Adams, Fair Haven soccer : After scoring once in a 6-1 playdown win over BFA-Fairfax, Adams fired in four goals as the No. 6 Slaters upset No. 3 Paine Mountain for a 4-1 triumph in the Division III quarterfinals.

Spencer Claussen, Leland & Gray soccer : After scoring two goals in a 3-0 win over Grace Christian in the playdowns, Claussen collected a goal and two assists in No. 6 Leland & Gray's 4-2 victory over No. 3 Caledonia United in the Division IV quarterfinals.

Nico Delena, Stowe cross-country running: The senior established a personal-best with a time of 16 minutes, 50.6 seconds to claim the Division III individual crown at the state championship meet at Thetford Academy.

Aden Galiano, Rutland football: The senior hauled in nine catches for 193 yards including the game-winning touchdown pass on fourth down in the final minute as Rutland bested Middlebury 22-21.

Gavin Huntington-Monroe, St. Johnsbury football: The sophomore went 12 of 23 through the air for 322 yards and five touchdowns, guiding St. Johnsbury to a 48-14 win over rival Lyndon in the 121st meeting of "The Game."

Ethan Leo, Essex soccer: After registering a hat trick to set the program's all-time career goals mark (47) in a 4-0 playdown win over Burlington, the senior struck four more times as No. 5 Essex edged No. 5 BFA-St. Albans, 5-4, in the Division I quarterfinals.

Evan Xia, South Burlington volleyball: Xia rose for 27 kills in No. 4 South Burlington's four-set victory over No. 5 Mount Mansfield in the quarterfinal round.
